title.zh: 卷一百二十六 列傳第五十一 魏盧李杜張韓
title.en: Volume 126 Biographies 51: Wei, Lu, Li, Du, Zhang, Han
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 列傳第五十一 魏盧李杜張韓 Volume 126 Biographies 51: Wei, Lu, Li, Du, Zhang, Han

sentences.zh: 魏盧李杜張韓

translations.literal: Wei, Lu, Li, Du, Zhang, Han
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Lu, Li, Du, Zhang, and Han

sentences.zh: 魏知古

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyang
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyang

sentences.zh: 魏知古，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyang was a man of Luze in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyang came from Luze in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 方直有雅才，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Upright and elegant in talent, he was elevated to the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Known for his rectitude and refined ability, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 以著作郎修國史，累遷衛尉少卿，檢校相王府司馬。

translations.literal: As Academician he compiled the national history, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Insignia and Acting Marshal of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Academician compiling the dynastic history, then rose through posts including Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Insignia and acting marshal of the Prince of Xiang's establishment.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，為吏部侍郎，以母喪解。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong reign he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, but resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服除，為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was made prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，以故屬拜黃門侍郎，兼修國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, because of former ties he was appointed Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong came to the throne, owing to their prior connection he was named Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate and again charged with revising the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 會造金仙、玉真觀，雖盛夏，工程嚴促，知古諫曰：「臣聞『古之君人，必時視人之所勤，人勤於力則功築罕，人勤於財則貢賦少，人勤於食則百事廢』。

translations.literal: When the Golden Immortal and Jade True abbeys were being built, though it was midsummer the work was urgently pressed. Zhiyang remonstrated, saying: "Your subject has heard that 'the ancient ruler of men must constantly observe what the people are busy with; if the people are busy with labor, few achievements can be built; if they are busy with wealth, few tributes and levies come in; if they are busy with food, a hundred affairs are neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When construction began on the Golden Immortal and Jade True abbeys, the work was driven hard even in midsummer. Zhiyang remonstrated: "I have heard that ancient rulers always watched what kept their people occupied: when the people were worn down by labor, little could be built; when they were drained by wealth, tribute and levies dwindled; when they were consumed by food production, everything else fell into neglect.

sentences.zh: 故曰『不作無益害有益』。

translations.literal: Thus it is said, 'Do nothing useless that harms the useful.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: do nothing useless that harms what is useful.

sentences.zh: 又曰『罔咈百姓以從己之欲』。

translations.literal: It is also said, 'Do not thwart the hundred surnames to follow your own desires.'
translations.idiomatic: And it is said: do not deceive and thwart the common people to satisfy your own wishes.

sentences.zh: 《禮》：『季夏之月，樹木方盛，無有斬伐，不可以興土功。』

translations.literal: The Rites: 'In the fourth month of summer, when trees are in full growth, there must be no cutting down; one may not undertake earthworks.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites states: "In the last month of summer, when trees are in full leaf, there must be no felling; earthworks must not be undertaken."

sentences.zh: 此皆興化立治、為政養人之本也。

translations.literal: These are all the foundations of promoting transformation, establishing governance, administering the state and nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: All of these are the foundations of promoting reform, establishing good government, and nourishing the people through rule.

sentences.zh: 今為公主造觀，將以樹功祈福，而地皆百姓所宅，卒然迫逼，令其轉徙，扶老攜幼，剔椽發瓦，呼嗟道路。

translations.literal: Now in building abbeys for the princesses, you mean to plant merit and pray for blessings, yet the land is all where the hundred surnames dwell; suddenly they are pressed and compelled to relocate, carrying the old and leading the young, tearing off rafters and digging out tiles, wailing on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Now abbeys are being built for the princesses to accumulate merit and seek blessings, yet the sites are all homes of common people. They are suddenly driven out and forced to move, the old supported on canes and the young led by the hand, rafters torn away and tiles ripped up, lamenting in the streets.

sentences.zh: 乖人事，違天時，起無用之作，崇不急之務，群心震搖，眾口藉藉。

translations.literal: It violates human affairs, violates Heaven's seasons, raises useless works, exalts unurgent tasks; all hearts tremble, every mouth murmurs.
translations.idiomatic: This runs counter to human affairs and violates the season; useless projects are raised and unurgent tasks exalted. Hearts everywhere are shaken, and murmuring fills every mouth.

sentences.zh: 陛下為人父母，欲何以安之？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, as father and mother of the people — how do you wish to give them peace?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people — how do you intend to give them peace?

sentences.zh: 且國有簡冊，君舉必記，言動之微，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: Moreover the state has brief records; the ruler's every act must be recorded; can one not be cautious about the slightest word and deed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the state keeps records in which every act of the ruler is entered. Can one not be cautious about the slightest word or deed?

sentences.zh: 願下明詔，順人欲，除功役，收之桑榆，其失不遠。」

translations.literal: I beg that you issue a clear edict, follow the people's desires, halt the labor, gather it back in the evening — the error would not be far to remedy.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict, follow the people's wishes, and halt the labor. If you gather things back even at the day's end, the fault would not be far beyond remedy."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 復諫曰：「自陛下戡翦兇逆，保定大器，蒼生颙颙，以謂朝有新政。

translations.literal: He remonstrated again: "Since Your Majesty suppressed the fierce and rebellious and secured the great vessel, the dark masses look up eagerly, thinking the court has a new policy.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated again: "Since Your Majesty cut down the violent and rebellious and secured the great vessel of state, the common people have looked up eagerly, believing the court would pursue a new policy.

sentences.zh: 今風教頹替日益甚，府藏空屈，人力勞敝，營作無厓，吏員浸增，諸司試補、員外、檢校官已贏二千，太符之帛為殫，太倉之米不支。

translations.literal: Now customs and teaching decline daily; the treasury is empty and strained; human strength is worn and exhausted; construction is boundless; official posts gradually increase; trial appointees, supernumeraries, and acting officials in the various offices already exceed two thousand; the silks of the Grand Storehouse are exhausted, the rice of the Grand Granary cannot suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now customs and instruction decay further each day; the treasury stands empty and strained; the people are worn out by labor; construction knows no limit; official posts keep multiplying; trial appointees, supernumeraries, and acting officials in the various offices already exceed two thousand. The silks of the Grand Storehouse are spent, and the rice of the Grand Granary will not last.

sentences.zh: 臣前請停金仙、玉真，訖亦未止。

translations.literal: Your subject previously requested halting the Golden Immortal and Jade True projects, yet they have still not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: I previously asked that work on the Golden Immortal and Jade True abbeys be halted, yet it has still not ceased.

sentences.zh: 今前水後旱，五谷不立，繇茲向春，必甚饑饉，陛下欲何方以賑之？

translations.literal: Now floods come first and drought after; the five grains do not stand; from here toward spring there will surely be severe famine — by what means does Your Majesty intend to relieve it?
translations.idiomatic: Now floods have been followed by drought; the five grains will not take; from here until spring famine will surely be severe. By what means does Your Majesty intend to provide relief?

sentences.zh: 又突厥於中國為患自久，其人非可以禮義誠信約也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Turks have long been a trouble to China; their people cannot be bound by ritual, righteousness, sincerity, and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Turks have long been a scourge to China; their people cannot be restrained by ritual, righteousness, sincerity, and good faith.

sentences.zh: 雖遣使請婚，恐豺狼之心，弱則順伏，強則驕逆，月滿騎肥，乘中國饑虛，講親際會，窺犯亭鄣，復何以防之？」

translations.literal: Though envoys are sent to request marriage, I fear the heart of wolves; when weak they submit, when strong they are arrogant and rebellious. When the moon is full and horses fat, seizing China's hunger and weakness at a marriage alliance, they will spy out and raid the border posts — how again shall we defend against them?
translations.idiomatic: Even if envoys come seeking marriage, I fear their wolfish nature: when weak they submit, when strong they grow arrogant and defiant. When the moon is full and their horses are fat, they will exploit China's hunger and weakness at the very moment of a marriage alliance, spy out our defenses, and raid the border posts. How then shall we guard against them?

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其直，以左散騎常侍同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his forthrightness and appointed him Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, with concurrent status as Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his frankness and appointed him Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with concurrent status as a third-rank official of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在春宮，又兼左庶子。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was in the Eastern Palace, Zhiyang also served concurrently as Left Guardian of the Heir.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was crown prince, Zhiyang also served concurrently as Left Guardian of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 所薦洹水令呂太一、蒲州司功參軍齊浣、右內率騎曹參軍柳澤、密尉宋遙、左補闕袁暉、右補闕封希顏、伊闕尉陳希烈，後皆有聞於時。

translations.literal: Those he recommended — Magistrate of Huanshui Lü Taiyi, Recorder of Pu Prefecture Qi Huan, Cavalry Section Aide of the Right Inner Guard Liu Ze, Commandant of Mi Song Yao, Left Remonstrance Official Yuan Hui, Right Remonstrance Official Feng Xiyan, and Magistrate of Yique Chen Xilie — all later won renown in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Among those he recommended were Lü Taiyi, magistrate of Huanshui; Qi Huan, recorder of Pu Prefecture; Liu Ze, cavalry aide of the Right Inner Guard; Song Yao, commandant of Mi; Yuan Hui, left remonstrance official; Feng Xiyan, right remonstrance official; and Chen Xilie, magistrate of Yique — all of whom later won renown in their day.

sentences.zh: 文宗大和二年，求其曾孫處訥，授湘陽尉，與魏徵、裴冕後擢任之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dahe of Emperor Wenzong, his great-grandson Chuna was sought out and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xiangyang, promoted along with the descendants of Wei Zheng and Pei Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dahe era under Emperor Wenzong, his great-grandson Chuna was sought out and appointed assistant magistrate of Xiangyang, promoted in the same manner as the descendants of Wei Zheng and Pei Mian.

sentences.zh: 盧懷慎

translations.literal: Lu Huaiyong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaiyong

sentences.zh: 盧懷慎，滑州人，蓋范陽著姓。

translations.literal: Lu Huaiyong was a man of Huazhou, of a distinguished clan of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaiyong came from Huazhou and belonged to a distinguished Fanyang clan.

sentences.zh: 祖悊，仕為靈昌令，遂為縣人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ti served as Magistrate of Lingchang and thus became a man of that county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ti served as magistrate of Lingchang and settled there as a local man.

sentences.zh: 懷慎在童草已不凡，父友監察御史韓思彥嘆曰：「此兒器不可量！」

translations.literal: Huaiyong was already extraordinary as a child; his father's friend Supervising Censor Han Siyan sighed and said: "This boy's capacity cannot be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child Huaiyong showed unusual promise. His father's friend, Supervising Censor Han Siyan, sighed and said, "This boy's capacity cannot be measured!

sentences.zh: 及長，第進士，歷監察御史。

translations.literal: When grown, he passed the jinshi examination and served successively as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he passed the jinshi examination and served as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era he was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was promoted to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 中宗謁武後上陽宮，後詔帝十日一朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong visited Empress Wu at Shangyang Palace; she ordered the Emperor to attend court once every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong visited Empress Wu at Shangyang Palace, she ordered him to attend court only once every ten days.

sentences.zh: 懷慎諫曰：「昔漢高帝受命，五日一朝太公於櫟陽宮，以起布衣登皇極，子有天下，尊歸於父，故行此耳。

translations.literal: Huaiyong remonstrated: "Formerly when Emperor Gaozu of Han received the Mandate, he attended the Grand Duke at Liyang Palace every five days — because rising from common cloth to the imperial apex, the son possessed all under Heaven and honor returned to the father, he acted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyong remonstrated: "When Emperor Gaozu of Han received the Mandate, he visited the Grand Duke at Liyang Palace every five days. That was because, having risen from commoner to emperor, the son held all under Heaven and honor rightly returned to the father. He acted only for that reason.

sentences.zh: 今陛下守文繼統，何所取法？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty guards the written tradition and succeeds to the line — what model do you take?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now guards the written tradition and succeeds to the legitimate line. What precedent do you follow?

sentences.zh: 況應天去提象才二里所，騎不得成列，車不得方軌，於此屢出，愚人萬有一犯屬車之塵，雖罪之何及。

translations.literal: Moreover from Yingtian to Tixiang is only about two li; horsemen cannot form ranks, chariots cannot run abreast. To go out repeatedly here — if some fool should once in ten thousand brush the dust of the imperial train, though you punish him what would it avail?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yingtian is only about two li from Tixiang; horsemen cannot form ranks and chariots cannot run abreast. To go out repeatedly on such a road — if some fool should once in ten thousand brush against the imperial train, no punishment afterward could undo the harm.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂宜遵內朝以奉溫清，無煩出入。」

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly thinks you should follow the inner court to perform warm and pure duties, without troubling yourself to go in and out.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view Your Majesty should attend the inner court to perform your filial duties and need not trouble yourself with going out.

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 遷右御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the Right Censorate.

sentences.zh: 上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth current affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞「善人為邦百年，可以勝殘去殺」。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard: "If good men govern the state for a hundred years, they can overcome cruelty and abolish killing."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that if good men govern the state for a hundred years, they can overcome cruelty and put an end to killing.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱：「茍用我者，期月而已，三年有成。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "If indeed you use me, in a full month it will suffice; in three years there will be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "If you would indeed employ me, in a full month there would be results; in three years there would be real achievement.

sentences.zh: 故《書》：「三載考績，三考黜陟幽明。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents: "After three years examine achievements; after three examinations promote the enlightened and demote the obscure."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents: "After three years examine achievements; after three examinations promote the capable and demote the incompetent."

sentences.zh: 昔子產相鄭，更法令，布刑書，一年人怨，思殺之，三年人德而歌之。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zichan was Chancellor of Zheng, he changed laws and orders and published penal writings; in one year the people resented him and thought of killing him; in three years the people cherished his virtue and sang of him.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly when Zichan served as chancellor of Zheng, he revised laws and published penal codes. After one year the people resented him and wished to kill him; after three years they cherished his virtue and sang his praise.

sentences.zh: 子產，賢者也，其為政尚累年而後成，況常材乎？

translations.literal: Zichan was a worthy man, yet his governing still required accumulated years before success — how much more ordinary talent?
translations.idiomatic: Zichan was a worthy man, yet his governance still required years before it succeeded. How much more must this be true of ordinary men?

sentences.zh: 比州牧、上佐、兩畿令或一二歲，或三五月即遷，曾不論以課最，使未遷者傾耳以聽，企踵以望，冒進亡廉，亦何暇為陛下宣風恤人哉？

translations.literal: Recently prefects, senior aides, and magistrates of the two capitals are transferred after one or two years, or three or five months, never judged by examination of merit. This makes those not yet transferred incline their ears to listen and stand on tiptoe to look forward; rushing advancement destroys integrity — when would they have leisure to spread Your Majesty's winds and show compassion to the people?
translations.idiomatic: Recently prefects, senior aides, and magistrates of the two metropolitan districts are transferred after only one or two years, or even three or five months, without regard to merit ratings. Those not yet transferred strain their ears to listen and stand on tiptoe in hope of promotion. Rushing for advancement destroys integrity. When would they have time to carry out Your Majesty's policies and show compassion to the people?

sentences.zh: 禮義不能興，戶口益以流，倉庫愈匱，百姓日敞，職為此耳。

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness cannot be raised; household registers daily drift away; storehouses grow ever emptier; the hundred surnames daily decline — the office is solely for this.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and righteousness cannot be revived; household registers grow ever more unstable; storehouses grow emptier; the common people grow poorer day by day — and the reason lies solely in this.

sentences.zh: 人知吏之不久，不率其教；

translations.literal: The people know officials will not stay long and do not follow their instruction;
translations.idiomatic: The people know officials will not remain long and do not follow their instruction;

sentences.zh: 吏知遷之不遙，不究其力。

translations.literal: officials know transfer is not far off and do not exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: officials know promotion is near and do not exhaust their strength.

sentences.zh: 俞處爵位，以養資望，雖明主有勤勞天下之誌，然僥幸路啟，上下相蒙，寧盡至公乎？

translations.literal: They are placed in ranks and titles to nurture seniority and reputation; though an enlightened ruler has the will to labor for all under Heaven, yet the path of lucky chance opens, above and below deceive one another — can there be full utmost fairness?
translations.idiomatic: Men are placed in offices merely to build seniority and reputation. Though an enlightened ruler may wish to labor for the realm, once the path of lucky advancement opens, superiors and subordinates deceive one another. How can perfect fairness be achieved?

sentences.zh: 此國病也。

translations.literal: This is the state's illness.
translations.idiomatic: This is a sickness of the state.

sentences.zh: 賈誼所謂蹠盩，乃小小者耳。

translations.literal: What Jia Yi called the robber Zhi and the rebel Dang are only small matters.
translations.idiomatic: What Jia Yi called the crimes of Zhi the robber and Dang the rebel are trifles by comparison.

sentences.zh: 此而不革，雖和、緩將不能為。

translations.literal: If this is not reformed, even He and Huan could not accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not reformed, even the physicians He and Huan could not cure it.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝綜核名實，興治致化，黃霸良二千石也，加秩賜金，就旌其能，終不肯遷。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han comprehensively examined names and realities, raised governance and brought transformation; Huang Ba was a good two-thousand-dan official — he was given added rank and bestowed gold, and his ability was marked in place, yet he was finally unwilling to be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han examined names against realities, promoted good government, and brought about reform. Huang Ba was an excellent prefect: he was given added rank and bestowed gold, and his ability was honored on the spot, yet he was never willing to accept transfer.

sentences.zh: 故古之為吏，至長子孫。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity those who served as officials often held office until their sons and grandsons succeeded them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in antiquity men who served as officials often held office long enough for sons and grandsons to succeed them.

sentences.zh: 臣請都督、刺史、上佐、畿令任未四考，不得遷。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that military commissioners, prefects, senior aides, and metropolitan magistrates who have not completed four examinations may not be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that military commissioners, prefects, senior aides, and metropolitan magistrates who have not completed four merit examinations not be transferred.

sentences.zh: 若治有尤異，或加賜車裘祿秩，降使臨問，璽書慰勉，須公卿闕，則擢之以勵能者。

translations.literal: If governance is exceptionally outstanding, either add gifts of carriage, fur robes, salary, and rank, send down envoys to inquire in person, or send sealed writings of consolation and encouragement; when a vacancy among dukes and ministers occurs, then promote them to encourage the capable.
translations.idiomatic: If governance is exceptionally outstanding, add gifts of carriage, fur robes, salary, and rank, send envoys to inquire in person, or issue sealed writings of encouragement. When a vacancy among high ministers occurs, promote such men to encourage the capable.

sentences.zh: 其不職或貪暴，免歸田裏，以明賞罰之信。

translations.literal: Those who are incompetent or greedy and violent should be dismissed to return to the countryside, to make clear the trustworthiness of rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are incompetent or greedy and violent should be dismissed to return to their fields, so that the credibility of rewards and punishments may be made clear.

sentences.zh: 昔唐、虞稽古，建官惟百。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang and Yu examined antiquity and established offices numbering only a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Tang and Yu looked back to the past and established only a hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 夏、商官倍，亦克用軿。

translations.literal: Under Xia and Shang offices doubled, yet they could still employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xia and Shang the number of offices doubled, yet the state could still employ them effectively.

sentences.zh: 此省官也。

translations.literal: This is reducing offices.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to reduce offices.

sentences.zh: 故曰「官不必備，惟其才」，「無曠庶官，天工人其代之。」

translations.literal: Thus it is said, "Offices need not all be filled — only their talent," and "Let no common office stand vacant; Heaven's work, men will replace it."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, "Offices need not all be filled — only their talent," and "Let no office stand vacant; Heaven's work, men will take it up."

sentences.zh: 此擇人也。

translations.literal: This is selecting men.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to select men.

sentences.zh: 今京諸司員外官數十倍，近古未有。

translations.literal: Now supernumerary officials in the capital offices number ten times the norm — nothing like this in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Today supernumerary officials in the capital offices number ten times the norm — nothing like this has been seen in recent antiquity.

sentences.zh: 謂不必備，則為有餘，求其代工，乃多不厘務，而奉稟之費，歲巨億萬，徙竭府藏，豈致治意哉」今民力敞極，河、渭廣漕，不給京師，公私耗損，邊隅未靜。

translations.literal: If one says offices need not all be filled, then there are surplus men; seeking them to replace work, many do not manage affairs, yet the cost of salaries and rations yearly reaches tens of millions — vainly draining the treasury. Is this the intent of bringing order?" Now the people's strength is utterly exhausted; the broad transport on the Yellow and Wei cannot supply the capital; public and private are worn down; the border regions are not yet calm.
translations.idiomatic: If offices need not all be filled, then there are surplus men; yet when one seeks them to take on work, many do not manage affairs at all, while salaries and rations cost tens of millions each year and vainly drain the treasury. Is this the intent of good government?" Today the people's strength is utterly exhausted; the broad transport on the Yellow and Wei cannot supply the capital; public and private resources are depleted; and the border regions are not yet calm.

sentences.zh: 儻炎暵成沴，租稅減入，疆場有警，賑救無年，何以濟之？

translations.literal: If heat and drought become calamity, rent and tax income diminish, the frontier has alarms, and relief has no surplus year — by what means shall we cross over?
translations.idiomatic: If heat and drought become calamity, tax revenues fall, the frontier is alarmed, and there is no surplus year for relief — how shall we cope?

sentences.zh: 「毋輕人事，惟艱；

translations.literal: "Do not slight human affairs — only difficulty;
translations.idiomatic: "Do not slight human affairs — only difficulty;

sentences.zh: 毋安闕位，惟危。」

translations.literal: do not rest secure in vacant posts — only peril.
translations.idiomatic: do not rest secure in vacant posts — only peril.

sentences.zh: 此慎微也。

translations.literal: This is being cautious in small matters.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to be cautious in small matters.

sentences.zh: 原員外之官，皆一時良幹，擢以才不申其用，尊以名不任其力，自昔用人，豈其然歟？

translations.literal: Originally supernumerary officials were all outstanding men of the time; promoted for talent yet not given scope for their use, honored by name yet not entrusted with their strength — from antiquity in employing men, has it ever been thus?
translations.idiomatic: Originally supernumerary posts were held by outstanding men of the day, promoted for talent yet not given scope to use it, honored by name yet not entrusted with real responsibility. Has employment of men ever been thus from antiquity?

sentences.zh: 臣請才堪牧宰上佐，並以遷授，使宣力四方，責以治狀。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that those whose talent suits prefects and senior aides all be appointed by transfer, sent to display their strength in the four quarters, and held accountable by records of governance.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that men capable of serving as prefects or senior aides be appointed by transfer, sent to exert themselves in the four quarters, and held accountable by their records of governance.

sentences.zh: 有老病若不任職者，一廢省之，使賢不肖確然殊貫，此切務也。

translations.literal: Those who are old or ill and cannot hold office should all be abolished and reduced, so that worthy and unworthy are clearly distinguished — this is an urgent task.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are old or ill and unfit for office should all be dismissed, so that the worthy and unworthy are clearly distinguished. This is an urgent task.

sentences.zh: 夫冒於寵賂，侮於鰥寡，為政之蠹也。

translations.literal: To be reckless in seeking favor and bribes, to insult widows and orphans — these are the vermin of governance.
translations.idiomatic: To be reckless in seeking favor and bribes and to mistreat widows and orphans are the vermin of good government.

sentences.zh: 竊見內外官有賕餉狼藉，劓剝蒸人，雖坐流黜，俄而遷復，還為牧宰，任以江、淮、嶺、磧，粗示懲貶，內懷自棄，徇貨掊貲，訖無悛心。

translations.literal: I have privately seen inner and outer officials with bribes scattered in disorder, flaying and stripping the common people; though sentenced to exile and dismissal, soon they are transferred back and again become prefects, assigned to the Yangtze, Huai, ranges, and deserts — only roughly showing punishment and demotion, yet inwardly abandoning themselves, pursuing goods and squeezing wealth, to the end without repentant hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen inner and outer officials who take bribes freely and flay the common people. Though sentenced to exile and dismissal, they are soon transferred back and again made prefects, assigned to the Yangtze, Huai, mountain ranges, and deserts — only nominally punished, yet inwardly resigned to their fate, pursuing profit and squeezing wealth, never repenting to the end.

sentences.zh: 明主之於萬物，平分而無偏施，以罪吏牧遐方，是謂惠奸而遺遠。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler toward the myriad things divides equally without partial favor; to send criminal officials to govern distant regions is called favoring the wicked and abandoning the remote.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler treats all things equally without partial favor. To send criminal officials to govern distant regions is to favor the wicked and abandon the remote.

sentences.zh: 遠州陬邑，何負聖化，而獨受其惡政乎？

translations.literal: Distant prefectures and remote districts — what have they done against sage transformation, that they alone should suffer such evil government?
translations.idiomatic: What have distant prefectures and remote districts done to deserve sage rule, that they alone should suffer such evil government?

sentences.zh: 邊僥之地，夷夏雜處，憑險恃遠易擾而難安；

translations.literal: In border and remote lands, barbarians and Chinese live mixed; relying on danger and distance, they are easily disturbed and hard to pacify;
translations.idiomatic: In border and remote regions barbarians and Chinese live mixed together; relying on rugged terrain and distance, they are easily disturbed and hard to pacify;

sentences.zh: 官非其才，則黎庶流亡，起為盜賊。

translations.literal: if officials are not matched to their talent, the black masses flee and rise as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: if officials lack the right talent, the common people flee and rise as bandits.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，不可用凡才，況猾吏乎？

translations.literal: From this it is said: ordinary talent cannot be used — how much less crafty officials?
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that ordinary talent cannot be used there — how much less crafty officials?

sentences.zh: 臣請以贓論廢者，削跡不數十年，不賜收齒。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that those dismissed on charges of corruption have their traces cut off for not several decades and not be granted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that those dismissed on charges of corruption be barred from office for decades and not be restored.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰「旌別淑慝」，即其誼也。

translations.literal: The Documents says, "Mark and distinguish the good and the evil" — this is its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Mark and distinguish the good from the evil" — that is the principle.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no response was given.

sentences.zh: 懷慎清儉不營產，服器無金玉文綺之飾，雖貴而妻子猶寒饑，所得祿賜，於故人親戚無所計惜，隨散輒盡。

translations.literal: Huaiyong was pure and frugal and did not build up property; his clothing and vessels had no ornament of gold, jade, brocade, or figured silk; though honored, his wife and children still suffered cold and hunger; whatever salary and gifts he received he spared nothing for old friends and kin, dispersing it all as soon as he got it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyong was pure and frugal and did not accumulate property. His clothing and utensils bore no gold, jade, brocade, or figured silk. Though he held high rank, his wife and children still knew cold and hunger. Whatever salary and gifts he received he gave freely to old friends and kin, dispersing it as soon as it came.

sentences.zh: 赴東都掌選，奉身之具，止一布囊。

translations.literal: When he went to the Eastern Capital to oversee selection, the goods for his person amounted to only one cloth sack.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to the Eastern Capital to oversee official selection, his personal belongings amounted to only one cloth sack.

sentences.zh: 既屬疾，宋璟、盧從願候之，見敞簀單藉，門不施箔。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Song Jing and Lu Congyuan visited him and saw open mats and a single matting, the door without bamboo screening.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Song Jing and Lu Congyuan visited him and found only bare mats and a single mat, with no bamboo screen on the door.

sentences.zh: 會風雨至，舉席自障。

translations.literal: When wind and rain came, he raised a mat to shield himself.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and rain came, he lifted a mat to shield himself.

sentences.zh: 日晏設食，蒸豆兩器、菜數杯而已。

translations.literal: At day's end he set out food — only two dishes of steamed beans and a few cups of vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: At day's end he served food — only two dishes of steamed beans and a few cups of vegetables.

sentences.zh: 臨別，執二人手曰：「上求治切，然享國久，稍倦於勤，將有憸人乘間而進矣。

translations.literal: On parting he took the two men's hands and said: "The sovereign seeks governance earnestly, yet having held the state long he grows somewhat weary of diligence; there will be crafty men who seize the interval and advance.
translations.idiomatic: As they parted he took their hands and said, "The sovereign earnestly seeks good government, yet having ruled long he grows somewhat weary of diligence. Crafty men will seize the opportunity and advance.

sentences.zh: 公第誌之！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen must remember this!
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must bear this in mind!

sentences.zh: 及治喪，家無留儲。

translations.literal: When the funeral was managed, the household had no remaining stores.
translations.idiomatic: When his funeral was arranged, the household had nothing left in store.

sentences.zh: 帝時將幸東都，四門博士張星上言：「懷慎忠清，以直道始終，不加優錫，無以勸善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital when Doctor of the Four Gates Zhang Xing submitted a statement: "Huaiyong was loyal and pure, following the straight path from beginning to end; if he is not given special rewards, there is no means to encourage goodness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital when Zhang Xing, Doctor of the Four Gates, submitted a memorial: "Huaiyong was loyal and pure and followed the straight path to the end. If he is not given special rewards, there will be no way to encourage goodness.

sentences.zh: 乃下制賜其家物百段，米粟二百斛。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued bestowing on his household a hundred lengths of goods and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued granting his household a hundred lengths of goods and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 帝後還京，因校獵、杜間，望懷慎家，環堵庳陋，家人若有所營者，馳使問焉，還白懷慎大祥，帝即以縑帛賜之，為罷獵。

translations.literal: Later when the Emperor returned to the capital, during a hunting expedition in the Du district he looked toward Huaiyong's house — the ring of walls was low and shabby, and the family seemed to be engaged in some undertaking. He sent a messenger at full speed to inquire; the reply came that Huaiyong was in the second year of mourning. The Emperor immediately bestowed silk and cloth and stopped the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor returned to the capital, during a hunt in the Du district he looked toward Huaiyong's house. The walls were low and shabby, and the family seemed busy with some task. He sent a messenger at once to inquire. The reply came that Huaiyong was observing the second year of mourning. The emperor immediately bestowed silk and cloth and called off the hunt.

sentences.zh: 經其墓，碑表未立，停蹕臨視，泫然流涕，詔官為立碑，令中書侍郎蘇颋為之文，帝自書。

translations.literal: Passing his tomb, he saw the stele and marker not yet erected; he halted the imperial carriage to look upon it, tears streaming down, and ordered officials to erect a stele, commanding Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting to compose the text, which the Emperor wrote in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Passing his tomb, he saw that no stele had yet been erected. He halted the imperial carriage to look upon it, tears streaming down his face, and ordered officials to erect a stele. He commanded Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting to compose the inscription, which the emperor wrote in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 子奐、弈。

translations.literal: His sons were Huan and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huan and Yi.

sentences.zh: 奐，早修整，為吏有清白稱。

translations.literal: Huan, from youth well ordered, as an official had the reputation of purity.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was well ordered from youth and as an official earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 歷御史中丞，出為陜州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Censor-in-Chief and went out as Prefect of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor-in-chief and was then appointed prefect of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十四年，帝西還，次陜，嘉其美政，題贊於聽事曰：「專城之重，分陜之雄，亦既利物，內存匪躬，斯為國寶，不墜家風。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan, the emperor returned west, halted at Shaan, praised his fine governance, and inscribed praise in the hall of audience, saying: "The weight of holding a city alone, the majesty of dividing Shaan — you have already benefited things; within you store not-self; this is a national treasure, not falling from the family wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Kaiyuan (736), when the emperor returned west and halted at Shaan, he praised Huan's excellent administration and inscribed a commendation in the provincial hall of audience: "The grave responsibility of governing a city on one's own, the proud station of the Shaan divide—you have already brought benefit to the people; in your heart you hold selfless devotion to duty. Such a man is a national treasure and preserves his family's honor.

sentences.zh: 尋召為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was summoned to court and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，為南海太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he served as Prefect of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era, he was appointed prefect of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 南海兼水陸都會，物產瑰怪，前守劉巨鱗、彭杲皆以贓敗，故以奐代之。

translations.literal: Nanhai was both a land and water metropolis; its products were rare and strange. The previous prefects Liu Julin and Peng Gao were both ruined by corruption, so Huan was appointed to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Nanhai was a great entrepôt by land and sea, rich in exotic goods. The previous prefects, Liu Julin and Peng Gao, had both been brought down by bribery, so Huan was sent to replace them.

sentences.zh: 汙吏斂手，中人之市舶者亦不敢幹其法，遠俗為安。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials withdrew their hands; even middlemen who traded in maritime shipping dared not interfere with his laws, and the distant customs were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials kept their hands to themselves, and even the brokers who handled maritime trade dared not circumvent his regulations; the distant region settled into peace.

sentences.zh: 時謂自開元後四十年，治廣有清節者，宋璟、李朝隱、奐三人而已。

translations.literal: At the time it was said that in the forty years since Kaiyuan, among those who governed Guang with integrity, only Song Jing, Li Chaoyin, and Huan — three men alone.
translations.idiomatic: People said that in the forty years since Kaiyuan, only three men who governed Guangzhou had maintained spotless integrity: Song Jing, Li Chaoyin, and Huan.

sentences.zh: 終尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 弈見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: Yi is treated in the "Biographies of the Loyal and Righteous."
translations.idiomatic: Yi is discussed in the Biographies of the Loyal and Righteous.

sentences.zh: 李元纮

translations.literal: Li Yuanhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhong

sentences.zh: 李元纮，字大綱，其先滑州人，後世占京兆萬年，本姓丙氏。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhong, courtesy name Dagang — his ancestors were men of Huazhou; later generations took up residence in Wannian of Jingzhao; their original surname was the Bing clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhong, courtesy name Dagang, came from a family originally of Huazhou that later settled in Wannian in the Jingzhao region; their original surname had been Bing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖粲，仕隋為屯衛大將軍，煬帝使督京師之西二十四郡盜賊，善撫循，能得士心。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Can served the Sui as General of the Garrison Guard. Emperor Yang had him supervise bandits and robbers in the twenty-four commanderies west of the capital. He was skilled at pacifying and tending and could win the hearts of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Can served the Sui as general of the garrison guard. Emperor Yang put him in charge of suppressing banditry in the twenty-four commanderies west of the capital. He was adept at winning people over and commanded the loyalty of local leaders.

sentences.zh: 高祖與之厚，及兵入關，以眾歸，授宗正卿、應國公，賜姓李。

translations.literal: Gaozu was close with him. When the army entered the Pass, he came over with his troops and was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Duke of Ying, and was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was on close terms with him. When the Tang army entered the Pass, Can submitted with his followers and was appointed director of the imperial clan court and Duke of Ying, and was granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 後為左監門大將軍，以其老，聽乘馬按視宮禁。

translations.literal: Later he became General of the Left Gate Guard. Because of his age, he was permitted to ride a horse while inspecting the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general of the Left Gate Guard. Because of his advanced age, he was allowed to ride horseback while inspecting the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘卒，謚曰明。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty years of age; his posthumous title was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties; his posthumous title was Ming.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，高宗時為太常卿、隴西公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuan, during Gaozong's reign, served as Minister of Ceremonies and Duke of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuan served under Gaozong as minister of ceremonies and Duke of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父道廣，武後時為汴州刺史，有善政。

translations.literal: His father Daoguang, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Prefect of Bianzhou and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoguang served under Empress Wu as prefect of Bianzhou and governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 突厥、契丹寇河北，議發河南兵擊之，百姓震擾，道廣悉心撫定，人無離散。

translations.literal: When the Turks and Khitan invaded Hebei, it was proposed to dispatch troops from Henan to attack them. The common people were shaken and disturbed. Daoguang devoted himself wholeheartedly to pacifying and settling them; no one dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks and Khitan raided Hebei, the court debated sending troops from Henan to repel them, and the populace was thrown into alarm. Daoguang worked tirelessly to calm the people, and none fled or scattered.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中監、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，封金城侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat and Concurrent Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrent associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秦州都督，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Military Commissioner of Qinzhou; posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed military commissioner of Qinzhou; his posthumous title was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 元纮，早修謹，仕為雍州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Yuanhong, from youth cultivated propriety and caution; in office he served as Registrar of the Revenue Section of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong was disciplined and conscientious from youth and entered service as registrar of the revenue section in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主勢震天下，百司順望風指，嘗與民競碾硙，元纮還之民。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping's power shook the world; the hundred offices all looked to her and followed her lead. She once competed with the people over millstones and waterwheels; Yuanhong returned them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Princess Taiping's power overshadowed the realm, and every office looked to her for direction. When she seized water mills and grinding stones from commoners, Yuanhong restored them to their owners.

sentences.zh: 長史竇懷貞大驚，趣改之，元纮大署判後曰：「南山可移，判不可搖也。」

translations.literal: The Chief Administrator Dou Huaizhen was greatly alarmed and hurried to change the decision. Yuanhong wrote in large characters after the judgment: "The southern mountains may be moved, but the judgment cannot be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator Dou Huaizhen was alarmed and rushed to reverse the ruling. Yuanhong wrote in bold characters at the end of the judgment: "The southern mountains may be moved, but this ruling shall not be altered.

sentences.zh: 改好畤令，遷潤州司馬，以辦治得名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Magistrate of Haochi, then promoted to Administrator of Runzhou — renowned for efficient governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Haochi, then promoted to administrator of Runzhou, where he won renown for efficient administration.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為萬年令，賦役稱平，擢京兆少尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, he served as Magistrate of Wannian; taxes and corvée were said to be fair, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as magistrate of Wannian, where taxes and corvée labor were judged equitable, and he was promoted to vice director of the capital prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔決三輔渠，時王、主、權家皆旁渠立硙，瀦堨爭利，元纮敕吏盡毀之，分溉渠下田，民賴其恩。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the opening of canals in the Three Assistants region. At the time, kings, princesses, and powerful families all set up millstones and waterwheels beside the canals, damming and blocking to fight for profit. Yuanhong ordered officials to destroy them all, divided the irrigation to fields below the canals, and the people relied on his grace.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the canals of the Three Assistants region cleared, princes, princesses, and powerful families had all built mills and dams along the waterways to monopolize the profits. Yuanhong ordered these structures demolished and the water redirected to irrigate the fields below; the people benefited greatly from his action.

sentences.zh: 三遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted three times, reaching Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會戶部楊玚、白知慎坐支調失宜，貶刺史，帝求可代者，公卿多薦元纮。

translations.literal: When the Ministers of Revenue Yang Chang and Bai Zhizhen were demoted to prefects for improper allocation and dispatch, the emperor sought someone who could replace them; the dukes and ministers mostly recommended Yuanhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers of revenue Yang Chang and Bai Zhizhen were demoted to prefects for mismanaging fiscal allocations, the emperor sought a replacement, and many senior officials recommended Yuanhong.

sentences.zh: 帝欲擢為尚書，宰相以資薄，乃為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to promote him to Director of a Ministry, but the chancellor said his qualifications were thin, so he was made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to promote him to director of a ministry, but the chief minister argued that his seniority was insufficient, and so he was appointed vice minister of revenue instead.

sentences.zh: 條陳利害及政得失，帝才之，謂可丞輔，賜衣一稱、絹二百匹。

translations.literal: He itemized advantages and harms and the gains and losses of government; the emperor recognized his talent and said he could serve as a chief minister, and bestowed upon him one suit of clothing and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted detailed memorials on fiscal policy and the strengths and weaknesses of administration. The emperor recognized his ability, declared him fit for the chancellorship, and granted him a suit of robes and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，封清水縣男。

translations.literal: The next year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingshui County.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Qingshui County.

sentences.zh: 元纮當國，務峻涯檢，抑奔競，誇進者憚之。

translations.literal: When Yuanhong held national power, he strove to make boundaries strict, suppressed rushing competition, and those who boasted for advancement feared him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanhong held power, he enforced strict standards, curbed the scramble for office, and those who flaunted their connections for promotion feared him.

sentences.zh: 五月五日，宴武成殿，賜群臣襲衣，特以紫服、金魚錫元纮及蕭嵩，群臣無與比。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month, a banquet was held at Wucheng Hall; the court granted robes to the ministers. Especially, purple robes and gold fish insignia were bestowed on Yuanhong and Xiao Song — none among the ministers were to be compared with them.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month the court held a banquet at Wucheng Hall and granted robes to the ministers. Yuanhong and Xiao Song alone received purple robes and gold fish insignia—honors unmatched by any other minister present.

sentences.zh: 是時，廢京司職田，議者欲置屯田。

translations.literal: At this time the metropolitan official fields were abolished, and discussants wished to establish garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the official salary fields of the capital bureaucracy had been abolished, and some officials proposed establishing garrison-agriculture colonies instead.

sentences.zh: 元纮曰：「軍國不同，中外異制，若人閑無役，地棄不墾，以閑手耕棄地，省饋運，實軍糧，於是有屯田，其為益尚矣。

translations.literal: Yuanhong said: "Military and civil affairs differ; inner and outer systems are not the same. If among the people there is no service levied and land is abandoned without cultivation, using idle hands to farm abandoned land, economizing transport of provisions, actually supplying military grain — for this there are garrison fields; their benefit is still great.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong said: "Military and civil administration follow different principles, and the inner and outer realms operate under different systems. Where the populace has no corvée burdens and land lies fallow, it makes sense to put idle labor to work on abandoned fields, cut transport costs, and fill military granaries—that is the purpose of garrison-agriculture colonies, and the benefit can be considerable.

sentences.zh: 今百官所廢職田不一縣，弗可聚也；

translations.literal: Now the abolished official fields of the hundred officials do not amount to one county; they cannot be gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: But the official fields now being abolished do not together amount to even one county—they cannot simply be consolidated.

sentences.zh: 百姓私田皆力自耕，不可取也。

translations.literal: The common people's private fields are all tilled by their own strength; they cannot be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The common people's private fields are all worked by their own labor and cannot be seized.

sentences.zh: 若置屯，即當公私相易，調發丁夫。

translations.literal: If garrison fields are established, then public and private must be exchanged and corvée laborers dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: If garrison colonies were established here, public and private land would have to be exchanged and corvée laborers conscripted.

sentences.zh: 調役則業廢於家，免庸則賦闕於國，內地為屯，古未有也。

translations.literal: When corvée is levied, then occupations are abandoned at home; when exemption from hired labor is granted, then tax assignments are lacking for the state. Garrison fields within the inner regions — in antiquity there never were such.
translations.idiomatic: Conscription would disrupt household livelihoods; exemptions from hired-service payments would leave the treasury short. Establishing garrison colonies in the heartland—nothing like this exists in precedent.

sentences.zh: 恐得不補失，徒為煩費。」

translations.literal: I fear the gain will not compensate for the loss; it will be vain trouble and expense.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the gains would not offset the losses and the scheme would only create needless expense and trouble.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: And so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，左庶子吳兢為史官，撰《唐書》及《春秋》，未成，以喪解，後上書請畢其功，詔許就集賢院成書；

translations.literal: Initially, Left Censor Wu Jing was a historiographer and compiled the "Book of Tang" and the "Spring and Autumn Annals" — unfinished; because of mourning he resigned; afterward he submitted a memorial requesting to complete the work; an edict permitted him to finish the book at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu Jing, left censor and historiographer, had begun compiling the Book of Tang and a Spring and Autumn chronicle but left the work unfinished when he resigned to observe mourning. He later petitioned to complete it, and the emperor permitted him to finish the project at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 張說致仕，詔在家修史。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue retired from office; an edict ordered him to revise history at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue retired from office, an edict authorized him to continue editing history from his home.

sentences.zh: 元纮因言：「國史記人君善惡、王政損益，褒貶所系，前聖尤重。

translations.literal: Yuanhong thereupon said: "The national history records the good and evil of rulers, the gains and losses of royal government — praise and blame depend upon it; former sages especially valued it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong then said: "The national history records the virtues and failings of rulers and the gains and losses of royal governance. Praise and blame hang upon it, and the sages of old held it in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 今國大典，分散不一，且太宗別置史館禁中，所以秘嚴之也。

translations.literal: Now the great canon of the state is scattered and not unified. Moreover, Taizong separately established the History Office within the palace — the reason was to keep it secret and strict.
translations.idiomatic: Today our great historical records are scattered and disorganized. Taizong established a separate History Office within the palace precisely to keep the work confidential and secure.

sentences.zh: 請勒說以書就館，參會撰錄。」

translations.literal: I request an order that Yue bring his books to the office and jointly compile and record.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Zhang Yue be ordered to bring his manuscripts to the History Office and join the collective compilation.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 後與杜暹不協，數辨爭帝前，帝不懌，皆罷之，以元纮為曹州刺史，徙蒲州，引疾去。

translations.literal: Later he and Du Xian were not in accord; repeatedly they argued before the emperor. The emperor was displeased and dismissed them both. Yuanhong was made Prefect of Caozhou, transferred to Puzhou, and resigned citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanhong fell out with Du Xian, and the two repeatedly quarreled before the emperor. Displeased, the emperor dismissed them both. Yuanhong was appointed prefect of Caozhou, then transferred to Puzhou, where he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 後以戶部尚書致仕，復起為太子詹事。

translations.literal: Later he retired as Minister of Revenue; he was recalled and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired as minister of revenue but was recalled to serve as grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少傅，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent; his posthumous title was Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 元纮再世宰相，有清節，其當國累年，未嘗改治第宅，僮馬敝弱，得封物赒給親族。

translations.literal: Yuanhong's family produced chancellors for two generations; he had integrity. While he held national power for accumulated years, he never altered or expanded his residence; his servants and horses were worn and weak; what he received from enfeoffment he used to aid his kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhong came from a family that had produced chancellors for two generations and was known for his integrity. Throughout his years in power he never renovated or expanded his residence; his servants and horses were shabby. What he received from his enfeoffment he gave away to support his relatives.

sentences.zh: 宋璟嘗嘆曰：「李公引宋遙之美，黜劉晃之貪，為國相，家無留儲，雖季文子之德，何以加之！」

translations.literal: Song Jing once sighed: "Lord Li promoted the worthy Song Yao and dismissed the greedy Liu Huang. As chief minister of the state, his house had no stored surplus — even the virtue of Ji Wenzi, how could one add to it!"
translations.idiomatic: Song Jing once sighed and said: "Lord Li elevated the worthy Song Yao and removed the greedy Liu Huang. As chief minister he kept nothing in store at home—even the virtue of Ji Wenzi could hardly surpass his!"

sentences.zh: 杜暹，濮州濮陽人。

translations.literal: Du Xian, a man of Puyang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian was a native of Puyang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父承誌，武後時為監察御史。

translations.literal: His father Chengzhi, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengzhi served under Empress Wu as supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 懷州刺史李文柬為人所告，詔承誌推驗，無實。

translations.literal: Li Wenjian, Prefect of Huaizhou, was reported by someone; an edict ordered Chengzhi to investigate; there was no substance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenjian, prefect of Huaizhou, was denounced by an accuser. An edict ordered Chengzhi to investigate, and he found no basis for the charge.

sentences.zh: 文柬，宗室近屬也，卒得罪，承誌貶為方義令，遷天官員外郎。

translations.literal: Wenjian was a near kinsman of the imperial clan; in the end he was punished. Chengzhi was demoted to Magistrate of Fangyi and transferred to Outside Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjian was a close kinsman of the imperial clan and was ultimately punished anyway. Chengzhi was demoted to magistrate of Fangyi, then transferred to outside director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 見羅織獄興，移疾去，卒於家。

translations.literal: When Luo Ji's prison prosecutions arose, he resigned citing illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Ji's wave of fabricated prosecutions began, he resigned on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 自高祖至暹，五世同居。

translations.literal: From Gaozu down to Xian, five generations lived together under one roof.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of Gaozu down to Xian, five generations of the family lived together under one roof.

sentences.zh: 暹尤恭謹，事繼母孝。

translations.literal: Xian was especially respectful and cautious and served his stepmother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was especially respectful and dutiful and served his stepmother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，補婺州參軍，秩滿歸，吏以紙萬番贐之，暹為受百番，眾嘆曰：「昔清吏受一大錢，何異哉？」

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Staff Member of Wuzhou. When his term ended and he returned, the clerks presented him with ten thousand sheets of paper as a farewell gift. Xian accepted only one hundred sheets. The crowd sighed: "In old times an incorrupt official accepted one large coin — how is this different?
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed staff member in Wuzhou. When his term ended and he departed, the clerks offered him ten thousand sheets of paper as a parting gift. Xian accepted only one hundred. Onlookers marveled: "The incorrupt official of old accepted but a single large coin—is this not the same spirit?

sentences.zh: 為鄭尉，復以清節顯。

translations.literal: As Assistant Magistrate of Zheng, he again distinguished himself for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant magistrate of Zheng, he again won distinction for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 華州司馬楊孚，公挺人也，每咨重暹。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, Administrator of Huazhou — a man of upright public character — always consulted and esteemed Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, administrator of Huazhou, was a man of upright character who always sought Xian's counsel and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 會孚遷大理正，暹適以累當坐，孚曰：「使若人得罪，眾安勸乎？」

translations.literal: When Fu was transferred to Senior Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Xian happened to face cumulative offenses and ought to have been punished. Fu said: "If such a man were punished, would the multitude be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: When Fu was promoted to senior judge of the Court of Judicial Review, Xian happened to face accumulated charges that would normally warrant punishment. Fu said: "If a man like this were punished, what encouragement would that offer the rest?

sentences.zh: 以狀言執政，繇是擢為大理評事。

translations.literal: He presented a memorial stating this to those in power; thereby Xian was promoted to Judicial Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial to the chief ministers making this argument, and Xian was thereupon promoted to judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，以監察御史覆屯磧西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, as Supervising Censor he went to review garrison fields west of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he served as supervising censor inspecting garrison-agriculture colonies west of the desert.

sentences.zh: 會安西副都護郭虔瓘與西突厥可汗阿史那獻、鎮守使劉遐慶更相訟，詔暹即按。

translations.literal: When Vice Protector-General of Anxi Guo Qianjin and the Western Turk Qaghan Ashina Xian and Garrison Commissioner Liu Xiaqing sued each other in turn, an edict ordered Xian to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Protector-General of Anxi Guo Qianjin, the Western Turk qaghan Ashina Xian, and garrison commissioner Liu Xiaqing brought counter-accusations against one another, an edict ordered Du Xian to investigate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 入突騎施帳，究索左驗。

translations.literal: He entered the tents of the Turgesh and thoroughly searched for evidence on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the tents of the Turgesh and exhaustively gathered evidence from both sides.

sentences.zh: 虜以金遺暹，暹固辭，左右曰：「公使絕域，不可失戎心。」

translations.literal: The barbarians presented gold to Xian; Xian firmly declined. Those at his side said: "My lord, you were sent to a distant region — you cannot lose the hearts of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen offered gold to Xian, but he firmly refused. His attendants urged him: "My lord, you have been sent to a distant frontier—you cannot afford to alienate these tribes.

sentences.zh: 乃受焉，陰埋幕下。

translations.literal: So he accepted it and secretly buried it beneath the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore accepted the gift but secretly buried it beneath the tent.

sentences.zh: 已出境，乃移文畀取之。

translations.literal: After he had crossed the border, he sent a written notice to have it retrieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had crossed the border, he sent an official notice requesting that the gold be dug up and returned.

sentences.zh: 突厥大驚，度磧追，不及，去。

translations.literal: The Turks were greatly alarmed; they crossed the desert in pursuit but could not catch up and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were astonished. They crossed the desert in pursuit but could not overtake him and turned back.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，以母喪解。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary; he resigned because of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary but resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 會安西都護張孝嵩遷太原尹，或言暹往使安西，虜伏其清，今猶慕思，乃奪服拜黃門侍郎兼安西副大都護。

translations.literal: When Protector-General of Anxi Zhang Xiaosong was transferred to Grand Governor of Taiyuan, some said that since Xian had previously served as envoy to Anxi the barbarians submitted to his integrity and still yearned for him, he was therefore released from mourning and appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Concurrent Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Protector-General of Anxi Zhang Xiaosong was transferred to grand governor of Taiyuan, some argued that because Xian had previously served in Anxi and the tribes still respected his integrity and yearned for his return, he should be recalled from mourning and appointed vice director of the Yellow Gate and concurrent vice protector-general of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，於闐王尉遲朒約突厥諸國叛，暹覺其謀，發兵討斬之，支黨悉誅，更立君長，於闐遂安。

translations.literal: The next year, King Yuchi Ou of Khotan plotted rebellion with the Turk states; Xian detected the scheme, sent troops to attack and behead him; all his partisans were executed; a new ruler was installed; Khotan was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year King Yuchi Ou of Khotan plotted rebellion with several Turkic states. Xian uncovered the conspiracy, sent troops to attack and execute him, wiped out his followers, installed a new ruler, and Khotan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was granted the additional title of grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 守邊四年，撫戎練士，能自勤勵，為夷夏所樂。

translations.literal: He guarded the frontier for four years, pacifying the barbarians and drilling soldiers; he could encourage himself to diligence; both barbarians and Chinese rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: He guarded the frontier for four years, pacifying the tribes and drilling the troops with unremitting diligence, and was beloved by both barbarian and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 十四年，召同中書門下平章事，遣中使往迎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was summoned as Concurrent Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery; an imperial envoy was sent to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was summoned to serve as concurrent associate director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and an imperial envoy was dispatched to escort him to court.

sentences.zh: 謁見，賜絹二百、馬一匹、第一區。

translations.literal: On audience he was granted two hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and a first-rank mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Upon audience he was granted two hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and a first-rank residence.

sentences.zh: 與李元纮輕重不得，罷為荊州都督長史，歷魏州刺史、太原尹。

translations.literal: He and Li Yuanhong could not agree on relative rank; he was dismissed and made Chief Administrator of the military commission of Jingzhou, then served as Prefect of Weizhou and Grand Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to reconcile his standing with Li Yuanhong's in the chancellorship, he was removed and appointed chief administrator of the Jingzhou military commission, then served successively as prefect of Weizhou and grand governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝幸北都，進戶部尚書，許扈蹕。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Northern Capital, Xian was promoted to Minister of Revenue and permitted to accompany the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Northern Capital, Xian was promoted to minister of revenue and permitted to accompany the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 還，復東幸，以暹為京留守。

translations.literal: On the return, the emperor again traveled east; Xian was made capital guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the emperor traveled east again and appointed Xian capital guardian.

sentences.zh: 暹率當番衛士繕三宮城，浚池，督役不少懈。

translations.literal: Xian led the rotating palace guards to repair the walls of the three palaces, dredge the moat, and supervise labor without the slightest slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Xian led the rotating palace guards in repairing the walls of the three palaces and dredging the moats, supervising the work without the slightest slackening.

sentences.zh: 帝聞嘉之，數賜書褒勞，進禮部尚書，封魏縣侯。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard and commended this, he repeatedly sent letters of praise and reward; Xian was promoted to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this he repeatedly sent letters of commendation, promoted Xian to minister of rites, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 二十八年卒，贈尚書右丞相，遣使護喪，禁中出絹三百匹賜之，太常謚曰貞肅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died; posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; an envoy was sent to escort the funeral; three hundred bolts of silk were issued from the palace as a gift; the Ministry of Ceremonies gave the posthumous title Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he died. He was posthumously appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs; an envoy was sent to escort the funeral procession, and three hundred bolts of silk were granted from the palace. The Ministry of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Zhensu.

sentences.zh: 右司員外郎劉同升等以暹行忠孝，謚有未盡，博士裴總謂暹往以墨衰受命安西，雖勤勞於國，不得盡孝。

translations.literal: Outside Director Liu Tongsheng and others said that because Xian's conduct was loyal and filial, the posthumous title had not fully expressed this. Doctor Pei Zong said that Xian had previously accepted appointment to Anxi while wearing unhemmed mourning garb of ink — though he toiled for the state, he could not fully fulfill filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongsheng, outside director of the right bureau, and others argued that because Xian's conduct had been both loyal and filial, the posthumous title did not do him full justice. Doctor Pei Zong countered that Xian had once accepted appointment to Anxi while still in unhemmed ink-dyed mourning garb—though he had toiled for the state, he had not fully fulfilled his filial obligations.

sentences.zh: 其子列訴，帝更敕有司考定，卒謚貞孝。

translations.literal: His sons submitted an appeal in array; the emperor again ordered the officials to examine and determine; in the end the posthumous title was Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons submitted a formal appeal. The emperor ordered the officials to reconsider, and the posthumous title was ultimately fixed as Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 暹友愛，撫異母弟昱甚厚。

translations.literal: Xian was fraternal and affectionate; he treated his younger half-brother Yu with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was warm and affectionate by nature and treated his younger half-brother Yu with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 其為人少學術，故當朝議論，時時失淺薄。

translations.literal: As a man he had little learning; therefore when he discussed matters at court, he sometimes fell short and was shallow.
translations.idiomatic: He had little scholarly training, and in court debates his remarks sometimes lacked depth.

sentences.zh: 然能以公清勤約自將，亹為之，自弱冠誓不通親友獻遺，以終身。

translations.literal: Yet he could restrain himself with public-mindedness, integrity, diligence, and economy, exerting himself in this unceasingly; from his weak-crown years he vowed never to accept gifts from kin and friends — and kept this to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he held himself to public service, integrity, diligence, and frugality with unwavering discipline. From his youth he vowed never to accept gifts from friends or relatives, and he kept that vow to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 既卒，尚書省及故吏致賻，其子孝友一不受，以行暹素誌雲。

translations.literal: After he died, the Department of State Affairs and former subordinates sent funeral gifts; his son Xiaoyou accepted none of them, thereby carrying out Xian's lifelong purpose.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Department of State Affairs and his former subordinates sent funeral gifts, but his son Xiaoyou refused every one, honoring Xian's lifelong vow.

sentences.zh: 暹族子鴻漸。

translations.literal: Xian's clansman Hongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's clansman Hongjian.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸字之巽。

translations.literal: Hongjian's courtesy name was Zhixun.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian's courtesy name was Zhixun.

sentences.zh: 父鵬舉，與盧藏用隱白鹿山，以母疾，與崔沔同授醫蘭陵蕭亮，遂窮其術。

translations.literal: His father Pengju, together with Lu Zangyong, hid on Bailu Mountain. Because of his mother's illness, together with Cui Mian he studied medicine under Xiao Liang of Lanling and exhaustively mastered the art.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pengju lived in seclusion on Bailu Mountain with Lu Zangyong. When his mother fell ill, he and Cui Mian studied medicine under Xiao Liang of Lanling and mastered the art thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 歷右拾遺。

translations.literal: He served successively as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He served as right reminder at court.

sentences.zh: 玄宗東行河，因遊畋，上賦以風。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong traveled east along the River, he took the occasion to hunt; the emperor composed a fu to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong traveled east along the Yellow River and went hunting for sport, the emperor composed a fu poem to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 終安州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸第進士，解褐延王府參軍，安思順表為朔方判官。

translations.literal: Hongjian passed the Jinshi examination; upon first appointment he was Staff Member of the Prince of Yan's household; An Sishun recommended him as Aide to the military commission of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian passed the jinshi examination and upon entering service became a staff member in the household of the Prince of Yan. An Sishun recommended him as aide to the Shuofang military commission.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，皇太子按軍平涼，未知所適，議出蕭關趣豐安。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, the Crown Prince reviewed troops at Pingliang, not knowing where to go; it was proposed to exit through Xiaoguan toward Feng'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, the crown prince mustered troops at Pingliang but did not know which direction to take; some proposed marching out through Xiaoguan toward Feng'an.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸與六城水運使魏少遊、節度判官崔漪、支度判官盧簡金、關內鹽池判官李涵謀曰：「胡羯亂常，二京覆沒，太子治兵平涼，然散地難恃也。

translations.literal: Hongjian, together with the Six Cities Water Transport Commissioner Wei Shaoyou, military commission aide Cui Yi, supply aide Lu Jianjin, and Guannei Salt Pond aide Li Han, counseled: "The Hu and Jie are by nature rebellious; the two capitals are fallen. The Crown Prince is drilling troops at Pingliang, yet scattered territory is hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian, together with Wei Shaoyou, commissioner of the Six Cities water transport; Cui Yi, military commission aide; Lu Jianjin, supply aide; and Li Han, Guannei salt pond aide, counseled: "The barbarian tribes have risen in rebellion and both capitals have fallen. The crown prince is gathering troops at Pingliang, but this open country offers no secure footing.

sentences.zh: 今朔方制勝之會，若奉迎太子，西詔河、隴，北結回紇，回紇固與國，收其勁騎，與大兵合，鼓而南，雪社稷之恥，不亦易乎！」

translations.literal: Now Shuofang is a place where superiority can be achieved. If we welcome the Crown Prince, proclaim to the west among He and Long, ally to the north with the Uyghurs — the Uyghurs are a firm ally of the state — gather their fierce cavalry, combine with the great army, beat the drums and march south, and wipe away the shame of the altars of soil and grain — would this not be easy!
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang is now the strategic ground where victory can be won. If we welcome the crown prince there, send proclamations west to He and Long, and ally with the Uyghurs to the north—the Uyghurs are already firm allies of the dynasty—we could gather their fierce cavalry, join them with our main force, and march south with drums beating to avenge the realm's disgrace. Would that not be the easier path?

sentences.zh: 即具上兵馬招輯之勢，且錄軍資、器械、儲廥凡最，使涵詣平涼見太子，太子大悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fully submitted the situation of troops, horses, recruitment, and consolidation, and also recorded an inventory of military supplies, weapons, and stored grain; they sent Han to Pingliang to see the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately submitted a detailed report on troop strength, horses, and the prospects for recruitment and consolidation, along with a full inventory of military supplies, weapons, and stored provisions, and dispatched Li Han to Pingliang to present it to the crown prince. The crown prince was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 會裴冕至自河西，亦勸之朔方。

translations.literal: Just then Pei Mian arrived from Hexi, and he also counseled going to Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian had just arrived from Hexi and added his voice to those urging the crown prince toward Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 而鴻漸與漪至白草頓迎謁，說曰：「朔方天下勁兵，靈州用武地。

translations.literal: Then Hongjian and Yi went to Baicaodun to meet and greet him, and urged: "Shuofang has the empire's strongest troops; Lingzhou is a place for wielding arms.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian and Cui Yi went out to Baicaodun to meet the crown prince and spoke to him: "Shuofang holds the empire's finest soldiers, and Lingzhou is ground made for war.

sentences.zh: 今回紇請和，吐蕃結附，天下列城堅守，以待王命。

translations.literal: Now the Uyghurs request peace and the Tibetans have joined in alliance; walled cities throughout the realm hold firm and await the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs now seek peace, and Tibet has allied itself with the court. Cities across the land stand firm in their garrisons, waiting only for imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 縱為賊據，日夜望官軍，以圖收復。

translations.literal: Even those occupied by rebels look day and night for the official army, hoping for recovery.
