translations.idiomatic: Even where rebels hold sway, the people watch day and night for the imperial armies, longing for restoration.

sentences.zh: 殿下治兵長驅，逆胡不足滅也。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness drills troops and drives straight ahead, the rebellious barbarians are not enough to withstand destruction.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness marshals your forces and presses forward without halt, these rebellious invaders will scarcely survive your onslaught.

sentences.zh: 太子喜曰：「靈武我之關中，卿乃吾蕭何也。」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said delightedly: "Lingwu is my Guanzhong; you are my Xiao He."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied in delight: "Lingwu will be my Guanzhong, and you are my Xiao He."

sentences.zh: 久之，乃召鴻漸為尚書右丞、太常卿，充禮儀使。

translations.literal: After a long while, Hongjian was summoned as Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed Commissioner of Ritual Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Hongjian was summoned to serve as vice minister of the right in the Department of State Affairs and minister of imperial sacrifices, with the added duty of commissioner of ritual ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 泰、建二陵制度皆鴻漸綜正，以優，封衛國公。

translations.literal: The regulations for the tombs Tai and Jian were all comprehensively corrected by Hongjian; for his excellence he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian oversaw and set in order the ritual arrangements for the Tai and Jian imperial tombs. In recognition of his excellence, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 又建言：「《周官》：『兇荒殺禮。』

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "The Offices of Zhou states: 'In years of famine and disaster, rites are reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial: "The Offices of Zhou says, 'In times of famine and calamity, rites should be curtailed.

sentences.zh: 今承大亂，民人夷殘，其婚葬鹵簿，非於國有大功及二等以上親皆不許給。」

translations.literal: Now inheriting great disorder, the people are devastated; wedding and funeral processions — none may be granted except to those with great service to the state and relatives of the second rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: We inherit a realm torn by great upheaval, and the people lie in ruin. I propose that ceremonial escorts for weddings and funerals be granted only to those who have rendered outstanding service to the state, or to relatives within the second degree of mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial.

sentences.zh: 代宗廣德二年，以兵部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde under Emperor Daizong, as Vice Minister of War he became Grand Councilor with concurrent membership in the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangde era under Emperor Daizong, he was appointed vice minister of war and grand councilor with concurrent authority in the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 尋進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 崔旰殺郭英軿據成都，邛州牙將柏貞節、滬州牙將楊子琳、劍州牙將李昌膋以兵討旰，蜀、劍大亂。

translations.literal: Cui Kan killed Guo Yingpi and seized Chengdu; Ya generals Bo Zhenjie of Qiongzhou, Yang Zilin of Luzhou, and Li Changliao of Jianzhou raised troops to attack Kan; Shu and Jian fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Kan killed Guo Yingpi and seized Chengdu. Bo Zhenjie, a garrison officer of Qiongzhou; Yang Zilin of Luzhou; and Li Changliao of Jianzhou each raised troops against him, plunging Shu and the sword passes into chaos.

sentences.zh: 命鴻漸以宰相兼成都尹、山南西道劍南東川副元帥、劍南西川節度副大使往鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Hongjian was ordered, as Chancellor, concurrently to serve as Prefect of Chengdu, Deputy Commander of the Southwestern Circuit and Eastern Chuan of Jiannan, and Deputy Military Commissioner of Western Chuan of Jiannan, to go and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was ordered to serve simultaneously as chancellor, prefect of Chengdu, deputy commander of the Southwestern Circuit and Eastern Chuan in Jiannan, and deputy military commissioner of Western Chuan in Jiannan, and sent to restore order.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸性畏怯，無它遠略，而晚節溺浮圖道，畏殺戮。

translations.literal: Hongjian was by nature timorous and cowardly, without other far-reaching plans, and in his later years he was absorbed in the Buddhist way and feared killing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjian was by nature timid and lacking in broader strategic vision. In his later years he became deeply devoted to Buddhism and shrank from bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 及逾劍門，懲艾張獻誠敗，且憚旰雄武，先許以不死。

translations.literal: When he crossed Jianmen Pass, chastened by Zhang Xiancheng's defeat and also fearing Kan's martial prowess, he first promised him he would not be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Sword Gate Pass, shaken by Zhang Xiancheng's defeat and intimidated by Cui Kan's martial reputation, he first pledged that Kan would not be executed.

sentences.zh: 既見，禮遇之，不敢加譙責，反委以政，日與從事杜亞、楊炎縱酒高會，因薦旰為成都尹，而授貞節邛州刺史，子琳滬州刺史，各罷兵。

translations.literal: Once they met, he treated Kan with courtesy, dared not add reproof, but instead entrusted him with government; day after day he feasted and drank with staff members Du Ya and Yang Yan; thereby he recommended Kan as Prefect of Chengdu, and appointed Zhenjie Prefect of Qiongzhou and Zilin Prefect of Luzhou, each disbanding their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When they met he treated Cui Kan with full courtesy, never daring to rebuke him, and instead handed over the reins of government. Day after day he caroused with his staff officers Du Ya and Yang Yan. He then recommended Cui Kan as prefect of Chengdu, appointed Bo Zhenjie prefect of Qiongzhou and Yang Zilin prefect of Luzhou, and had each of the rival commanders stand down their forces.

sentences.zh: 乃請入朝，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested to enter court; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested leave to return to court, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及見帝，盛言旰威略可任，宜為留後。

translations.literal: When he saw the emperor, he spoke at length of Kan's martial prowess and capacity, saying he should be kept as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared before the emperor, he spoke at length of Cui Kan's military talent and declared him fit to serve as regional military governor.

sentences.zh: 獻寶器五床、羅錦十五床，麝臍五石。

translations.literal: He presented five couches of precious vessels, fifteen couches of silk brocade, and five shi of musk navel.
translations.idiomatic: He presented five sets of precious vessels, fifteen sets of brocaded silks, and five shi of musk.

sentences.zh: 復輔政。

translations.literal: He again assisted in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed his role in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 議者疾其長亂。

translations.literal: Critics hated him for prolonging disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Critics condemned him for prolonging the chaos.

sentences.zh: 進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年，兼東都留守、河南淮西山南東道副元帥，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dali, concurrently Eastern Capital Garrison Commander and Deputy Commander of Henan, Huai West, and Eastern Circuit of Southwestern Mountains, he declined on grounds of illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Dali era he was also named eastern capital garrison commander and deputy commander of Henan, Huai West, and the Eastern Circuit of the Southwestern Mountains, but pleaded illness and declined to take up the posts.

sentences.zh: 又讓山南、劍南副元帥，聽之。

translations.literal: He also yielded the deputy command of Southwestern Mountains and Jiannan; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also relinquished his deputy command over the Southwestern Mountains and Jiannan circuits, and the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾甚，辭宰相，罷三日卒，年六十一，贈太尉，謚曰文憲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, gravely ill, he resigned as Chancellor; three days after removal he died, age sixty-one; posthumously made Grand Marshal; posthumous title Wendian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, gravely ill, he resigned from the chancellorship and died three days later at the age of sixty-one. He was posthumously appointed grand marshal and given the posthumous title Wendian, "Cultivated and Lawful."

sentences.zh: 鴻漸自蜀還，食千僧，以為有報，搢紳效之。

translations.literal: When Hongjian returned from Shu, he fed a thousand monks, believing there would be reward; gentry and officials emulated this.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjian returned from Shu, he feasted a thousand monks, believing the act would bring karmic reward, and officials throughout the court followed his example.

sentences.zh: 病甚，令僧剔項發，遺命依浮圖葬，不為封樹。

translations.literal: When gravely ill, he had monks shave his head; his final instructions were to be buried according to Buddhist rites, without mound or trees.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he had monks shave his head, and left instructions to be buried in the Buddhist manner, without a mound or planted trees.

sentences.zh: 張九齡

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling

sentences.zh: 張九齡，字子壽，韶州曲江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, courtesy name Zishou, was a man of Qujiang in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, courtesy name Zishou, was a native of Qujiang in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 七歲知屬文，十三以書幹廣州刺史王方慶，方慶嘆曰：「是必致遠。」

translations.literal: At seven he could compose linked prose; at thirteen he submitted a letter to the Prefect of Guangzhou Wang Fangqing; Fangqing sighed and said: "This one will surely reach far.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already compose polished prose. At thirteen he sent a letter to Wang Fangqing, prefect of Guangzhou, who exclaimed, "This boy is destined for great things.

sentences.zh: 會張說謫嶺南，一見厚遇之。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Yue was demoted to Lingnan; on first meeting him he treated Jiuling warmly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was demoted to the south, he met Jiuling and immediately took a strong liking to him.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀，庭中木連理。

translations.literal: While mourning his father, his grief was destructive; in the courtyard trees joined in shared trunk.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father his grief was so consuming that trees in the courtyard fused together at the trunk — a prodigy of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，始調校書郎，以道侔伊呂科策高第，為左拾遺。

translations.literal: He was advanced in the jinshi examination; first appointed Proofreader; through high standing in the "Paths Equal to Yi and Lü" examination he became Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was first assigned as a proofreader. He scored at the top of the special "Paths Equal to Yi and Lü" examination and was appointed left reminder.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗即位，未郊見，九齡建言：

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Xuanzong had ascended but had not yet performed the suburban rite; Jiuling memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had recently taken the throne but had not yet performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven. Jiuling submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 天，百神之君，王者所由受命也。

translations.literal: Heaven is lord of the hundred spirits; it is by Heaven that the king receives mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is sovereign over all the spirits; it is through Heaven that a ruler receives the mandate to rule.

sentences.zh: 自古繼統之主，必有郊配，蓋敬天命，報所受也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, rulers who inherited succession always performed suburban sacrifice and matching rites — it is to revere Heaven's mandate and repay what was received.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity every ruler who inherited the throne has performed the suburban rites, honoring Heaven's mandate and acknowledging the charge Heaven has conferred.

sentences.zh: 不以德澤未洽，年谷未登，而闕其禮。

translations.literal: One does not omit the rite because benevolent influence is not yet widespread, or the year's grain harvest is not yet abundant.
translations.idiomatic: One must not omit these rites simply because benevolent rule has not yet permeated every corner of the realm, or because the harvest has not yet been plentiful.

sentences.zh: 昔者周公郊祀後稷以配天，謂成王幼沖，周公居攝，猶用其禮，明不可廢也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou performed suburban sacrifice to Houji to match Heaven; though King Cheng was young and the Duke of Zhou held regency, he still used the rite — showing clearly it cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Duke of Zhou sacrificed to Houji at the suburban altar to accompany Heaven. Even when King Cheng was still a child and the duke ruled as regent, he upheld these rites — proof that they must never be set aside.

sentences.zh: 漢丞相匡衡曰：「帝王之事，莫重乎郊祀。」

translations.literal: Chancellor Kuang Heng of Han said: "Among a ruler's affairs, nothing is weightier than suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Han chancellor Kuang Heng said, "Of all a ruler's duties, none outweighs the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒亦言：「不郊而祭山川，失祭之序，逆於禮，故《春秋》非之。」

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu also said: "To sacrifice to mountains and rivers without suburban rite loses the order of sacrifice, is contrary to rites — therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns it."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu likewise argued that offering sacrifices to mountains and rivers without first performing the suburban rite violates the proper order of worship and offends ritual propriety — which is why the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns the practice.

sentences.zh: 臣謂衡、仲舒古之知禮。

translations.literal: Your subject considers Heng and Zhongshu knowers of rites in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, Heng and Zhongshu were among antiquity's true masters of ritual.

sentences.zh: 皆以郊之祭所宜先也。

translations.literal: Both held that the suburban sacrifice ought to come first.
translations.idiomatic: Both understood that the suburban sacrifice must come first.

sentences.zh: 陛下紹休聖緒，於今五載，而未行大報，考之於經，義或未通。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has continued the sacred line; it is now five years, yet the great responsive sacrifice has not been performed — examined against the classics, the propriety may not be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited a sacred line of succession, yet five years have passed without performing the great responsive sacrifice to Heaven. Measured against the classics, this may fall short of what is proper.

sentences.zh: 今百谷嘉生，鳥獸鹹若，夷狄內附，兵革用弭，乃怠於事天，恐不可以訓。

translations.literal: Now the hundred grains grow well, birds and beasts all thrive, barbarians submit inward, weapons are at rest — yet one is slack toward serving Heaven; I fear this cannot be instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred grains flourish, birds and beasts thrive, distant peoples submit, and arms lie still — yet we neglect our duty to Heaven. I fear this sets a poor example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 願以迎日之至，升紫壇，陳采席，定天位，則聖典無遺矣。

translations.literal: I wish that on the day of welcoming the sun you ascend the purple altar, lay out colored mats, fix Heaven's position — then the sage canon will lack nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that on the day of the winter solstice Your Majesty ascend the purple altar, lay out the ceremonial mats, and take your ordained place before Heaven — so that no element of the sage rites be left unperformed.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He further stated:
translations.idiomatic: He further argued:

sentences.zh: 乖政之氣，發為水旱。

translations.literal: The qi of misaligned governance manifests as flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: When governance goes awry, its corruption takes the form of flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 天道雖遠，其應甚邇。

translations.literal: Though Heaven's Way is distant, its response is very near.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way may seem distant, but its response is swift and close at hand.

sentences.zh: 昔東海枉殺孝婦，天旱久之。

translations.literal: Formerly in Donghai a filial woman was wrongly killed; drought lasted long.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago in Donghai a filial woman was unjustly executed, and drought followed for a long season.

sentences.zh: 一吏不明，匹婦非命，則天昭其冤。

translations.literal: One clerk was unenlightened; one common woman died untimely — then Heaven disclosed her injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When a single magistrate errs in judgment and one innocent woman dies, Heaven itself reveals the wrong.

sentences.zh: 況六合元元之眾，縣命於縣令，宅生於刺史，陛下所與共治，尤親於人者乎！

translations.literal: How much more the myriad masses of the six directions — their lives hang on the county magistrate, their livelihood rests on the prefect; are these not those with whom Your Majesty jointly governs, most intimate with the people!
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for the countless common people of the realm, whose lives depend on county magistrates and whose livelihood rests with prefects — the very officials with whom Your Majesty shares the work of governance and who stand closest to the people!

sentences.zh: 若非其任，水旱之繇，豈唯一婦而已。

translations.literal: If they are not fit for their posts, the source of flood and drought — is it only one woman?
translations.idiomatic: When unfit men hold these posts, the source of flood and drought is scarcely confined to a single wronged woman.

sentences.zh: 今刺史，京輔雄望之郡，猶少擇之，江、淮、隴、蜀、三河大府之外，稍非其人。

translations.literal: Now for prefects — even for the capital districts and commanderies of lofty reputation selection is still limited; beyond the Yangzi, Huai, Long, Shu, and the three Yellow River circuits, many are not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Even for prefects of the capital region and other prestigious commands, selection remains lax. Beyond the Yangzi, Huai, Long, Shu, and the three Yellow River circuits, many posts are held by unsuitable men.

sentences.zh: 繇京官出者，或身有累，或政無狀，用牧守之任。

translations.literal: Those who come from capital officials — some have personal encumbrances, some have no worthy performance in governance — yet are used for prefect and garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Men dispatched from the capital include some burdened by personal scandals and others with no record of competent administration, yet they are assigned to prefectural and garrison commands.

sentences.zh: 為斥逐之地。

translations.literal: These posts serve as places of rejection and exile.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial office has become a dumping ground for the cast aside.

sentences.zh: 或因附會以忝高位，及勢衰，謂之不稱京職，出以為州。

translations.literal: Or through faction they shamefully reach high rank, and when influence wanes they are said to be unfit for capital office and sent out as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Others claw their way to high rank through factional maneuvering; when their influence fades they are declared unfit for capital service and packed off to a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武夫、流外，積資而得，不計於才。

translations.literal: Military men and those from outside the regular flow, by accumulated seniority obtain posts, talent not counted.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and men from irregular clerical backgrounds accumulate seniority until they win appointment, with no regard for actual ability.

sentences.zh: 刺史乃爾，縣令尚可言哉？

translations.literal: Prefects are thus — can county magistrates even be spoken of?
translations.idiomatic: If this is the state of prefectural appointment, what hope is there for county magistrates?

sentences.zh: 氓庶，國家之本，務本之職，乃為好進者所輕，承弊之民，遭不肖所擾，聖化從此銷郁，繇不選親人以成其敝也。

translations.literal: The common people are the state's foundation; posts devoted to the foundation are yet scorned by those eager to advance; people inheriting decay suffer disturbance from unworthy men; sage transformation from this withers — the source is not selecting close-to-people men, completing this corruption.
translations.idiomatic: The common people are the foundation of the state, yet the offices devoted to serving them are treated with contempt by the ambitious. The afflicted populace suffers under unworthy magistrates, and imperial virtue withers — all because close contact with the people is no longer valued in selection.

sentences.zh: 古者刺史入為三公，郎官出宰百里。

translations.literal: In antiquity prefects entered office as the Three Dukes; court gentlemen went out to govern a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity prefects rose to become one of the Three Dukes, and palace officers went out to govern counties.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷士入而不出，其於計私，甚自得也。

translations.literal: Now court scholars enter and do not go out; in reckoning private gain they are quite self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Today court officials enter service and never leave the capital; in calculating their private advantage they find this arrangement entirely satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 京師衣冠所聚，身名所出，從容附會，不勤而成，是大利在於內，而不在於外也。

translations.literal: The capital is where robes and caps gather, where body and name emerge; at ease in faction, without labor succeeding — the great profit lies within, not without.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is where officials gather and reputations are made. Through leisurely networking and facile alliances one can advance without exertion. The real rewards lie inside the capital walls, not beyond them.

sentences.zh: 智能之士，欲利之心，安肯復出為刺史、縣令哉？

translations.literal: Men of ability and wisdom, with hearts desiring profit — how would they again go out as prefect and county magistrate?
translations.idiomatic: Able and ambitious men, bent on advancement, will scarcely volunteer to serve again as prefects or magistrates in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 國家賴智能以治，而常無親人者，陛下不革以法故也。

translations.literal: The state relies on able men to govern, yet constantly lacks men close to the people — because Your Majesty has not reformed through law.
translations.idiomatic: The state depends on capable men for good governance, yet we perpetually lack officials who truly know the people — because Your Majesty has not reformed the system by statute.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂欲治之本，莫若重守令，守令既重，則能者可行。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly considers that the root of desiring governance lies in nothing so much as honoring prefects and magistrates; once prefects and magistrates are honored, then able men can act.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit that the foundation of good governance lies in elevating the status of prefects and magistrates. Once those offices carry real weight, able men will step forward to fill them.

sentences.zh: 宜遂科定其資：凡不歷都督、刺史，雖有高第，不得任侍郎、列卿；

translations.literal: It is fitting immediately to fix qualifications by statute: all who have not served as regional commander or prefect, though with high grades, may not hold Vice Minister or ministry posts;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes should be enacted at once: no one who has not served as a regional commander or prefect may hold a vice-ministerial post or head a ministry, regardless of examination rank;

sentences.zh: 不歷縣令，雖有善政，不得任臺郎、給、舍；

translations.literal: those who have not served as county magistrate, though with good governance, may not hold Secretariat gentlemen, draft reviewers, or palace secretaries;
translations.idiomatic: no one who has not served as a county magistrate may hold a post as a palace secretary, draft reviewer, or attendant — however distinguished his record;

sentences.zh: 都督、守、令雖遠者，使無十年任外。

translations.literal: For regional commanders, prefects, and magistrates even in distant places, let none hold high office without ten years of service outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Even for the most distant commanderies and counties, no one should reach high office without at least ten years of service outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 如不為此而救其失，恐天下猶未治也。

translations.literal: If without doing this one remedies their failures, I fear the realm will still not be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we act on this, I fear the realm will never be truly well governed.

sentences.zh: 又古之選士，惟取稱職，是以士修素行，而不為僥幸，奸偽自止，流品不雜。

translations.literal: Again, in antiquity selection of scholars took only fitness for office; thus scholars cultivated plain conduct and did not seek luck; fraud ceased of itself, ranks were not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity officials were chosen solely on fitness for office. Scholars therefore cultivated genuine virtue and did not chase fortune; deceit ceased on its own and ranks stayed pure.

sentences.zh: 今天下不必治於上古，而事務日倍於前，誠以不正其本而設巧於末也。

translations.literal: Now the realm need not be governed like high antiquity, yet affairs daily double what came before — truly because the root is not corrected while ingenuity is deployed at the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Our realm need not match the governability of high antiquity, yet the burden of administration grows daily — precisely because we neglect the root and apply clever fixes only at the margins.

sentences.zh: 所謂末者，吏部條章，舉贏千百。

translations.literal: What are called the branches: the Ministry of Personnel's articles and regulations — they run to thousands upon thousands.
translations.idiomatic: These marginal fixes are the Ministry of Personnel's regulations, which now run to thousands upon thousands of clauses.

sentences.zh: 刀筆之人，溺於文墨；

translations.literal: Men of brush and document drown in paperwork;
translations.idiomatic: Clerks drown in paperwork;

sentences.zh: 巧史猾徒，緣奸而奮。

translations.literal: cunning clerks and slippery fellows, riding on deceit, rise up.
translations.idiomatic: while cunning scribes and unscrupulous manipulators exploit the system to advance themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂始造簿書，備遺忘耳，今反求精於案牘，而忽於人才，是所謂遺劍中流，契丹以記者也。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that records were first made merely to guard against forgetfulness; now one instead seeks precision in dossiers while neglecting human talent — this is what is called dropping the sword in midstream and marking the boat to find it.
translations.idiomatic: Records were originally kept merely as aides-mémoire. Now we demand perfection in paperwork while neglecting human talent — like the man who dropped his sword in the river and marked the spot on his boat's rail, thinking he could recover it later.

sentences.zh: 凡稱吏部能者，則曰自尉與主簿，繇主簿與丞，此執文而知官次者也，乃不論其賢不肖，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: All who praise the Ministry's competence say: from aide and chief clerk, through chief clerk to assistant magistrate — this is grasping documents and knowing official order; yet worth and unworth are not discussed — is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Those who praise the Ministry's competence speak of orderly promotion from aide and chief clerk to assistant magistrate — promoting by paperwork and rank alone, with no regard for merit. Can anything be more absurd?

sentences.zh: 夫吏部尚書、侍郎，以賢而授者也，豈不能知人？

translations.literal: The Minister and Vice Ministers of Personnel are conferred because they are worthy — can they not know men?
translations.idiomatic: The minister and vice ministers of the Ministry of Personnel are appointed for their discernment — are they incapable of judging men?

sentences.zh: 如知之難，拔十得五，斯可矣。

translations.literal: If knowing is difficult, selecting ten and getting five — that would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Even if judging talent is difficult, selecting five worthy men from ten candidates would be accomplishment enough.

sentences.zh: 今膠以格條，據資配職，為官擇人，初無此意，故時人有平配之誚，官曹無得賢之實。

translations.literal: Now stuck to grid articles, assigning posts by seniority — choosing men for offices was originally not this intent; thus contemporaries have the mockery of "level assignment"; official bureaus obtain no reality of worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Today appointments are frozen by rigid regulations and matched to seniority alone. The original intent — choosing the right man for each office — has been lost. People mock this as "level assignment," and the bureaus gain no genuinely capable officials.

sentences.zh: 臣謂選部之法，敝於不變。

translations.literal: Your subject considers the Selection Bureau's method is exhausted by unchanging.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that the Selection Bureau's methods have grown obsolete through inflexibility.

sentences.zh: 今若刺史、縣令精核其人，則管內歲當選者，使考才行，可入流品，然後送臺，又加擇焉，以所用眾寡為州縣殿最，則州縣慎所舉，可官之才多，吏部因其成，無庸人之繁矣。

translations.literal: Now if prefects and magistrates scrutinize their men, then within their jurisdictions those due for annual selection — have them examine ability and conduct, those who may enter the flowing ranks, then send to the Secretariat for further selection; use the number employed as lesser-or-greater ranking of prefectures and counties — then prefectures and counties will be careful in whom they recommend, capable-for-office talent will be many, the Ministry of Personnel will follow what is already accomplished, and there will not be the tangle of useless men.
translations.idiomatic: If prefects and magistrates were charged with rigorously assessing local candidates each year, testing their ability and character before sending qualified men to the capital for final review, and if prefectures and counties were ranked according to how many capable officials they produced, local authorities would take recommendations seriously. Talent worthy of office would multiply, and the Ministry of Personnel could build on work already done, without the present tangle of unsuitable appointees.

sentences.zh: 今歲選乃萬計，京師米物為耗，豈多士哉？

translations.literal: Now annual selection runs to ten thousand; capital rice and goods are consumed — is this many scholars?
translations.idiomatic: Annual selection now draws tens of thousands to the capital, depleting the city's grain and goods. Are these truly so many worthy men?

sentences.zh: 蓋冒濫抵此爾。

translations.literal: Generally fraud and overflow reach this only.
translations.idiomatic: In truth they are mostly impostors and mediocrities who have slipped through.

sentences.zh: 方以一詩一判，定其是非，適使賢人遺逸，此明代之闕政也。

translations.literal: Yet with one poem and one judgment their right and wrong is fixed — just causing worthy men to be overlooked; this is a lacuna in policy of an enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet appointment still hinges on a single poem and a single legal judgment. Worthy men are passed over — a glaring flaw in an otherwise enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 天下雖廣，朝廷雖眾，必使毀譽相亂，聽受不明，事則已矣。

translations.literal: Though the realm is broad and the court numerous, one necessarily lets slander and praise become confused, hearing and accepting unclearly — and with that the matter is finished.
translations.idiomatic: For all the breadth of the realm and the size of the court, we allow reputation and slander to become hopelessly confused. With no clear basis for judgment, selection becomes arbitrary — and that is where the matter ends.

sentences.zh: 如知其賢能，各有品第，每一官缺，不以次用之，豈不可乎？

translations.literal: If knowing their worth and ability, each having rank grades, for each office vacancy not using by order of sequence — would this not be acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: If we truly knew each man's ability and assigned clear rank to each, then when a post fell vacant we could appoint by merit rather than seniority — would that not be better?

sentences.zh: 如諸司要官，以下等叨進，是議無高卑，唯得與不爾。

translations.literal: If for vital posts of various bureaus, inferior grades shamelessly advance — then deliberation has no high or low, only obtaining or not.
translations.idiomatic: When men of inferior rank push into key posts across the ministries, debate over suitability collapses into a simple question of who gets the job and who does not.

sentences.zh: 故清議不立，而名節不修，善士守誌而後時，中人進求而易操也。

translations.literal: Thus pure discourse is not established, fame and integrity are not cultivated; good men hold purpose but fall behind the times, middling men advance seeking and easily change conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Pure discourse ceases to matter, and integrity goes unrewarded. Good men hold to their principles and are passed over; mediocre men chase advancement and readily abandon their standards.

sentences.zh: 朝廷能以令名進人，士亦以修名獲利，利之出，眾之趨也。

translations.literal: If the court can through fine name advance men, scholars also through cultivating name obtain profit; profit emerges — the multitude's direction.
translations.idiomatic: If the court promoted men on the strength of genuine reputation, scholars would cultivate reputation to advance — and where profit lies, the multitude will follow.

sentences.zh: 不如此，則小者得於茍求，一變而至阿私；

translations.literal: If not thus, then petty men gain through shameless seeking, one change leading to private favoritism;
translations.idiomatic: Without this, petty men win advancement through shameless maneuvering, and the first step toward cronyism is taken;

sentences.zh: 大者許以分義，再變而成朋黨矣。

translations.literal: greater men promised partial righteousness, a second change becoming faction cliques.
translations.idiomatic: while greater men trade on sham principle, and the second step leads straight to factional cliques.

sentences.zh: 故於用人不可不第其高下，高下有次，則不可以妄幹，天下之士必刻意修飾，而刑政自清，此興衰之大端也。

translations.literal: Thus in employing men one cannot fail to grade high and low; when high and low have order, then one cannot recklessly interfere; scholars under Heaven will surely deliberately cultivate and adorn themselves, and punishments and governance will naturally clear — this is the great hinge of rise and decline.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing officials we cannot fail to rank men by ability. When ranks are clear and ordered, unqualified men cannot force their way in. Scholars everywhere will cultivate themselves deliberately, law and governance will naturally improve — and this is the decisive hinge between a dynasty's rise and decline.

sentences.zh: 俄遷左補闕。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to left supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 九齡自才鑒，吏部試拔萃與舉者，常與右拾遺趙冬曦考次，號稱詳平。

translations.literal: Jiuling himself had talent for judging; for the Ministry's "Outstanding Selection" examination with candidates, he often ranked them with Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi, called detailed and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling had a keen eye for talent. When grading candidates for the Ministry of Personnel's "Outstanding Selection" examination, he often worked alongside Right Reminder Zhao Dongxi; their judgments were renowned for thoroughness and fairness.

sentences.zh: 改司勛員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Outer Gentleman of the Bureau of Merit Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer gentleman of the Bureau of Merit Records.

sentences.zh: 時張說為宰相，親重之，與通譜系，常曰：「後出詞人之冠也。」

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Yue was Chancellor; he held Jiuling close and valued him, connected through clan registry; he often said: "Among later-generation men of letters, the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue was then serving as chancellor and held Jiuling in high regard; they were connected through shared clan ties. Zhang often declared, "He stands at the head of the younger generation of writers.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人內供奉，封曲江男，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Drafting Officer Inner Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Qujiang, advanced to Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretariat drafting officer with inner-attendant status, enfeoffed as Baron of Qujiang, and promoted to full secretariat drafting officer.

sentences.zh: 會帝封泰山，說多引兩省錄事主書及所親攝官升山，超階至五品。

translations.literal: When the Emperor performed Feng at Mount Tai, Yue greatly introduced chief clerks and record keepers of the two secretariats and his own favorites holding temporary posts to ascend the mountain, leapfrogging ranks to fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, Zhang Yue arranged for numerous record clerks from both secretariats and his own protégés holding temporary posts to join the ascent, promoting them by leaps to the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 九齡當草詔，謂說曰：「官爵者，天下公器，先德望，後勞舊。

translations.literal: When Jiuling was drafting an edict, he said to Yue: "Offices and ranks are the public instruments of the realm; first come virtue and reputation, then merit and senior service.
translations.idiomatic: While drafting an edict, Jiuling said to Zhang Yue: "Offices and ranks belong to the realm, not to private favor. Virtue and standing must come first; only then merit and long service.

sentences.zh: 今登封告成，千載之絕典，而清流隔於殊恩，胥史乃濫章韨，恐制出，四方失望。

translations.literal: Now the Feng and Shan rites have been completed — a millennial rite of surpassing solemnity — yet the pure stream is shut off by special favor, and clerks and recorders indiscriminately receive insignia. I fear that once the edict is issued, disappointment will spread throughout the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Feng and Shan rites have just been completed — a once-in-a-millennium ceremony — yet men of pure reputation are passed over for special favors while clerks and petty officials receive insignia indiscriminately. Once this edict goes out, the realm will be deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 方進草，尚可以改，公宜審計。」

translations.literal: The draft is not yet submitted; it can still be changed. Your Excellency should consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The draft has not yet been submitted — it can still be revised. Your Excellency should weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「事已決矣，悠悠之言不足慮。」

translations.literal: Yue said: "The matter is already decided. Idle talk is not worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied: "The matter is settled. Idle gossip is not worth heeding."

sentences.zh: 既而果得謗。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he indeed came in for slander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he did indeed become the target of slander.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宇文融方事田法，有所關奏，說輒建議違之。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong was then implementing the field-tax law and submitted related memorials; whenever he did, Yue would propose measures contrary to them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Yuwen Rong was then pushing his field-tax reforms and submitting related memorials. Whenever he did, Yue would propose countermeasures.

sentences.zh: 融積不平，九齡為言，說不聽。

translations.literal: Rong grew increasingly resentful. Jiuling spoke on his behalf, but Yue would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's resentment mounted. Jiuling pleaded on his behalf, but Yue would not listen.

sentences.zh: 俄為融等痛詆，幾不免，九齡亦改太常少卿，出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Yue was fiercely denounced by Rong and others and nearly ruined. Jiuling was also transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and sent out as prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yue was savagely attacked by Rong and his allies and nearly destroyed. Jiuling was transferred to vice minister of ceremonies and sent out as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 以母不肯去鄉里，故表換洪州都督。

translations.literal: Because his mother refused to leave their home district, he petitioned to be transferred to military commissioner of Hongzhou instead.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother would not leave their home district, he petitioned to be reassigned as military commissioner of Hongzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 徙桂州，兼嶺南按察選補使。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Guizhou, concurrently serving as commissioner for inspection and selection in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Guizhou, concurrently serving as Lingnan commissioner for inspection and official selection.

sentences.zh: 始說知集賢院，嘗薦九齡可備顧問。

translations.literal: When Yue first directed the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, he had once recommended Jiuling as fit to serve as a court adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue first directed the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, he had recommended Jiuling as a man fit to serve as a court adviser.

sentences.zh: 說卒，天子思其言，召為秘書少監、集賢院學士，知院事。

translations.literal: When Yue died, the emperor recalled his recommendation and summoned Jiuling to serve as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and director of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue died, the emperor remembered his recommendation and summoned Jiuling to serve as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and director of the academy.

sentences.zh: 會賜渤海詔，而書命無足為者，乃召九齡為之，被詔輒成。

translations.literal: When an edict was to be sent to Bohai and no one among the drafting staff was adequate for the task, Jiuling was summoned to write it. Given the commission, he completed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict was needed for Bohai and no one in the drafting office was up to the task, Jiuling was summoned to write it. He received the commission and finished it on the spot.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Works and put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of works and put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 數乞歸養，詔不許，以其弟九臯、九章為嶺南刺史，歲時聽給驛省家。

translations.literal: He repeatedly petitioned to return home to support his mother. The edict refused, but appointed his brothers Jiugao and Jiuzhang as prefects of Lingnan and allowed them post horses each year to visit their family.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked leave to return home and care for his mother. The court refused, but appointed his brothers Jiugao and Jiuzhang as prefects in Lingnan and allowed them post horses each year to visit the family.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，以母喪解，毀不勝哀，有紫芝產坐側，白鳩、白雀巢家樹。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, he resigned upon his mother's death. His grief was so extreme it threatened his health. A purple lingzhi fungus appeared beside his seat, and white doves and white magpies nested in the trees at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, he resigned when his mother died. His grief was so overwhelming it threatened his life. A purple lingzhi mushroom sprouted beside his seat, and white doves and white magpies nested in the trees at his home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，奪哀拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: That year, before mourning was complete, he was recalled to serve again as vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: That year, before the mourning period had ended, he was recalled to serve as vice director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined; permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined; the emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷中書令。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 始議河南開水屯，兼河南稻田使。

translations.literal: He first proposed opening water-colony farms in Henan and concurrently served as commissioner for Henan rice fields.
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed establishing water-colony farms in Henan and concurrently served as commissioner for Henan rice fields.

sentences.zh: 上言廢循資格，復置十道采訪使。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne to abolish advancement by fixed seniority and restore the ten-circuit investigative commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne to abolish advancement by fixed seniority and restore the ten-circuit investigative commissioners.

sentences.zh: 李林甫無學術，見九齡文雅，為帝知，內忌之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu had no learning. Seeing Jiuling's literary elegance and the emperor's appreciation of him, he secretly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had no scholarly training. Seeing Jiuling's literary refinement and the emperor's esteem for him, he secretly resented him.

sentences.zh: 會范陽節度使張守珪以斬可突幹功，帝欲以為侍中。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Fanyang, achieved merit by beheading Ketugan, the emperor wished to appoint him Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Fanyang, won distinction by beheading Ketugan, the emperor wished to appoint him grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「宰相代天治物，有其人然後授，不可以賞功。

translations.literal: Jiuling said: "The chief minister governs affairs on Heaven's behalf. The post is granted only when there is a worthy man — it cannot be used to reward military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling said: "The chief minister governs on Heaven's behalf. The post is given only when there is a worthy man — it must not be used to reward military merit.

sentences.zh: 國家之敗，由官邪也。」

translations.literal: The ruin of a state comes from corrupt appointments.
translations.idiomatic: States fall when offices are filled wrongly.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「假其名若何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What if we grant him only the title?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What if we grant him only the title?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「名器不可假也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Names and insignia must not be lent.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Titles and insignia must not be lent out.

sentences.zh: 有如平東北二虜，陛下何以加之？」

translations.literal: If he pacifies the two barbarian foes of the northeast, how would Your Majesty reward him then?"
translations.idiomatic: If he pacifies the two barbarian powers of the northeast, how will Your Majesty reward him then?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The appointment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 又將以涼州都督牛仙客為尚書，九齡執曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The emperor next proposed appointing Niu Xianke, governor of Liangzhou, as Minister. Jiuling insisted: "That cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor next proposed appointing Niu Xianke, governor of Liangzhou, as minister. Jiuling objected: "That cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 尚書，古納言，唐家多用舊相，不然，歷內外貴任，妙有德望者為之。

translations.literal: The Minister is the ancient 'voice that receives words.' The Tang usually appoint former chief ministers; otherwise men who have held important posts at court and in the provinces, and who truly possess virtue and standing, fill the role.
translations.idiomatic: The minister is the ancient 'voice that receives words.' The Tang usually appoints former chief ministers; otherwise men who have held weighty posts at court and in the provinces and who truly possess virtue and standing.

sentences.zh: 仙客，河、湟一使典耳，使班常伯，天下其謂何？」

translations.literal: Xianke is merely an envoy from the He and Huang region. To place such a man in rank with the highest ministers — what would the world say?
translations.idiomatic: Xianke is only a frontier commissioner from the He and Huang region. To place such a man among the highest ministers — what would the realm say?

sentences.zh: 又欲賜實封，九齡曰：「漢法非有功不封，唐遵漢法，太宗之制也。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to grant actual fiefs. Jiuling said: "Han law holds that there is no enfeoffment without merit. The Tang follows Han law — this was Taizong's institution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also wished to grant him an actual fief. Jiuling said: "Han law holds that there is no enfeoffment without merit. The Tang follows Han law — this was Taizong's institution.

sentences.zh: 邊將積谷帛，繕器械，適所職耳。

translations.literal: A frontier general hoarding grain and cloth and repairing weapons is only doing his duty.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier general who stores grain and cloth and repairs weapons is only doing his duty.

sentences.zh: 陛下必賞之，金帛可也，獨不宜裂地以封。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must reward him, gold and silk will suffice. Cutting off territory for an enfeoffment is alone inappropriate."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must reward him, gold and silk will suffice. Carving off territory for an enfeoffment alone is inappropriate."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「豈以仙客寒士嫌之邪？

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Do you despise him because Xianke is a man of humble origin?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said: "Do you look down on him because Xianke is a man of humble origin?

sentences.zh: 卿固素有門閱哉？」

translations.literal: Surely you come from an illustrious lineage yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely you yourself come from an illustrious lineage?"

sentences.zh: 九齡頓首曰：「臣荒陬孤生，陛下過聽，以文學用臣。

translations.literal: Jiuling bowed his head and said: "I am a solitary man from a remote corner. Your Majesty overestimated me and employed me for my literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling bowed his head and said: "I am a solitary man from a remote corner. Your Majesty overestimated me and employed me for my literary ability.

sentences.zh: 仙客擢胥史，目不知書。

translations.literal: Xianke was promoted from clerk and record-keeper; he cannot even read.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke was promoted from clerk and record-keeper; he cannot even read.

sentences.zh: 韓信，淮陰一壯夫，羞絳、灌等列。

translations.literal: Han Xin was a mere stalwart from Huaiyin, yet he was ashamed to stand in the same rank as Zhou Bo and Guan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin was only a stalwart from Huaiyin, yet he was ashamed to stand in the same rank as Zhou Bo and Guan Ying.

sentences.zh: 陛下必用仙客，臣實恥之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty insists on using Xianke, I would truly be shamed."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty insists on using Xianke, I would truly be shamed."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 翌日，林甫進曰：「仙客，宰相材也，乃不堪尚書邪？

translations.literal: The next day Linfu came forward and said: "Xianke has the makings of a chief minister — is he unfit even to be Minister?
translations.idiomatic: The next day Linfu came forward and said: "Xianke has the makings of a chief minister — is he unfit even to be minister?

sentences.zh: 九齡文吏，拘古義，失大體。」

translations.literal: Jiuling is a literary clerk, bound by ancient precedent, missing the larger design.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling is a literary clerk, bound by ancient precedent, and misses the larger design.

sentences.zh: 帝由是決用仙客不疑。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore resolved to employ Xianke without further doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore resolved to employ Xianke without further hesitation.

sentences.zh: 九齡既戾帝旨，固內懼，恐遂為林甫所危，因帝賜白羽扇，乃獻賦自況，其末曰：「茍效用之得所，雖殺身而何忌？」

translations.literal: Having already crossed the emperor's wishes, Jiuling was inwardly afraid he might be endangered by Linfu. When the emperor bestowed a white-feather fan, he submitted a rhapsody presenting himself through it, its closing lines reading: "If only my service finds its proper place, what would I regret though my body were destroyed?
translations.idiomatic: Having already crossed the emperor's wishes, Jiuling was inwardly afraid he might be destroyed by Linfu. When the emperor bestowed a white-feather fan, he submitted a rhapsody presenting himself through it, its closing lines reading: "If only my service finds its proper place, what would I regret though my body were destroyed?

sentences.zh: 又曰：「縱秋氣之移奪，終感恩於篋中。」

translations.literal: And again: "Though autumn's chill may seize and take away, I would still be grateful within the casket."
translations.idiomatic: And again: "Though autumn's chill may seize and take away, I would still be grateful within the casket."

sentences.zh: 帝雖優答，然卒以尚書右丞相罷政事，而用仙客。

translations.literal: Though the emperor answered warmly, in the end Jiuling was removed from office as Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Xianke was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor answered warmly, in the end Jiuling was removed from office as right director of the Department of State Affairs and Xianke was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷士大夫持祿養恩矣。

translations.literal: From then on, court officials held their salaries and cultivated favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, court officials held their salaries and cultivated favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦長安尉周子諒為監察御史，子諒劾奏仙客，其語援讖書。

translations.literal: He had once recommended Zhou Ziliang, warden of Chang'an, as investigating censor. Ziliang impeached Xianke, citing prognostic texts in his language.
translations.idiomatic: He had once recommended Zhou Ziliang, warden of Chang'an, as investigating censor. Ziliang impeached Xianke, citing prognostic texts in his language.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，杖子諒於朝堂，流州，死於道。

translations.literal: The emperor in anger had Ziliang beaten in the Hall of Audience, banished to Zhou, and he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger had Ziliang beaten in the Hall of Audience, banished him to Zhou, and he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 九齡坐舉非其人，貶荊州長史。

translations.literal: Jiuling was punished for recommending an unworthy man and demoted to senior adjutant of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was punished for recommending an unworthy man and demoted to senior adjutant of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 雖以直道黜，不戚戚嬰望，惟文史自娛，朝廷許其勝流。

translations.literal: Though removed for following the straight path, he was neither downcast nor grasping after hope. He amused himself with history and literature alone, and the court acknowledged him among the leading men of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Though removed for following the straight path, he was neither downcast nor grasping after hope. He amused himself with history and literature alone, and the court acknowledged him among the leading men of his age.

sentences.zh: 久之，封始興縣伯，請還展墓，病卒，年六十八，贈荊州大都督，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: After some time he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shixing County. He requested leave to return and tend his family's graves, fell ill, and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously appointed grand governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was enfeoffed as baron of Shixing County. He requested leave to return and tend his family's graves, fell ill, and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously appointed grand governor of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 九齡體弱，有藉。

translations.literal: Jiuling's physique was weak and he used a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling's physique was weak and he used a staff.

sentences.zh: 故事，公卿皆搢笏於帶，而後乘馬。

translations.literal: By precedent, high ministers all tucked their court tablets into their belts before mounting their horses.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, high ministers all tucked their court tablets into their belts before mounting their horses.

sentences.zh: 九齡獨常使人持之，因設笏囊，自九齡始。

translations.literal: Jiuling alone regularly had someone carry his instead, and so the tablet case was devised — beginning with Jiuling.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling alone regularly had someone carry his for him, and so the tablet case was devised — beginning with Jiuling.

sentences.zh: 後帝每用人，必曰：「風度能若九齡乎？」

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever the emperor considered appointing someone, he would say: "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the emperor considered appointing someone, he would say: "Does his bearing match Jiuling's?

sentences.zh: 初，千秋節，公、王並獻寶監，九齡上「事鑒」十章，號《千秋金鑒錄》，以伸諷諭。

translations.literal: Early on, at the Longevity Festival, dukes and princes all presented treasure mirrors. Jiuling submitted ten chapters of "Mirrors of Affairs," titled Records of the Golden Mirrors of Longevity, to extend admonition and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, at the Longevity Festival, dukes and princes all presented treasure mirrors. Jiuling submitted ten chapters of "Mirrors of Affairs," titled Records of the Golden Mirrors of Longevity, to extend admonition and counsel.

sentences.zh: 與嚴挺之、袁仁敬、梁升卿、盧怡善，世稱其交能終始者。

translations.literal: With Yan Tingzhi, Yuan Renjing, Liang Shengqing, and Lu Yi he was on good terms; their age praised them for friendships that lasted to the end.
translations.idiomatic: With Yan Tingzhi, Yuan Renjing, Liang Shengqing, and Lu Yi he was on good terms; their age praised them for friendships that lasted to the end.

sentences.zh: 及為相，諤諤有大臣節。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, he remonstrated forthrightly and showed the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief minister, he remonstrated forthrightly and showed the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝在位久，稍怠於政，故九齡議論必極言得失，所推引皆正人。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had reigned long and had grown somewhat slack in governance. Jiuling therefore spoke out fully on what was right and wrong, and those he recommended were all upright men.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had reigned long and had grown somewhat slack in governance. Jiuling therefore spoke out fully on what was right and wrong, and those he recommended were all upright men.

sentences.zh: 武惠妃謀陷太子瑛，九齡執不可。

translations.literal: Consort Wu Hui plotted to bring down Crown Prince Ying. Jiuling firmly refused to go along.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu Hui plotted to bring down Crown Prince Ying. Jiuling firmly refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 妃密遣宦奴牛貴兒告之曰：「廢必有興，公為援，宰相可長處。」

translations.literal: The consort secretly sent the eunuch Niu Guier to tell him: "If one prince is deposed, another must rise. If you lend your support, the chancellorship can be yours for the long term.
translations.idiomatic: The consort secretly sent the eunuch Niu Guier to tell him: "If one prince is deposed, another must rise. If you lend your support, the chancellorship can be yours for the long term.

sentences.zh: 九齡叱曰：「房幄安有外言哉！」

translations.literal: Jiuling rebuked him: "How dare private words from the inner chambers reach the outside!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling rebuked him: "How dare private words from the inner chambers reach the outside!"

sentences.zh: 遽奏之，帝為動色，故卒九齡相而太子無患。

translations.literal: He immediately reported the matter. The emperor's expression changed, and so while Jiuling remained chief minister the crown prince suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately reported the matter. The emperor's expression changed, and so while Jiuling remained chief minister the crown prince suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 安祿山初以范陽偏校入奏，氣驕蹇，九齡謂裴光庭曰：「亂幽州者，此胡雛也。」

translations.literal: When An Lushan first came to court from Fanyang as a low-ranking garrison officer, his manner was arrogant and overbearing. Jiuling said to Pei Guangting: "The one who will bring disorder to Youzhou is this barbarian whelp.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan first came to court from Fanyang as a low-ranking garrison officer, his manner was arrogant and overbearing. Jiuling said to Pei Guangting: "The one who will bring disorder to Youzhou is this barbarian whelp.

sentences.zh: 及討奚、契丹敗，張守珪執如京師，九齡署其狀曰：「穰苴出師而誅莊賈，孫武習戰猶戮宮嬪，守珪法行於軍，祿山不容免死。」

translations.literal: When the campaign against the Xi and Khitan failed, Zhang Shougui had him bound and sent to the capital. Jiuling endorsed the petition: "When Rangju marched forth he executed Zhuang Jia; when Sun Wu drilled troops he still executed palace women. Shougui has enforced military law in the ranks — Lushan cannot be spared death."
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against the Xi and Khitan failed, Zhang Shougui had him bound and sent to the capital. Jiuling endorsed the petition: "When Rangju marched forth he executed Zhuang Jia; when Sun Wu drilled troops he still executed palace women. Shougui has enforced military law in the ranks — Lushan cannot be spared death."

sentences.zh: 帝不許，赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor refused and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 九齡曰：「祿山狼子野心，有逆相，宜即事誅之，以絕後患。」

translations.literal: Jiuling said: "Lushan has the heart of a wolf cub — he bears the countenance of rebellion. He should be executed on the spot to forestall future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling said: "Lushan has the heart of a wolf cub — he bears the countenance of rebellion. He should be executed on the spot to forestall future trouble.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿無以王衍知石勒而害忠良。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yan who knew of Shi Le, harm the loyal and worthy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do not, like Wang Yan who knew of Shi Le, harm the loyal and worthy."

sentences.zh: 卒不用。

translations.literal: In the end his advice was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his advice was not taken.

sentences.zh: 帝後在蜀，思其忠，為泣下，且遣使祭於韶州，厚幣恤其家。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor was in Shu, he thought of Jiuling's loyalty, wept, and sent an envoy to offer sacrifices at Shaozhou, with generous gifts to comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor was in Shu, he thought of Jiuling's loyalty, wept, and sent an envoy to offer sacrifices at Shaozhou, with generous gifts to comfort his family.

sentences.zh: 開元後，天下稱曰曲江公而不名雲。

translations.literal: After the Kaiyuan era, the realm called him the Duke of Qujiang rather than speak his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaiyuan era, the realm called him the Duke of Qujiang rather than speak his personal name.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，德宗賢其風烈，復贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Emperor Dezong admired his sterling character and again posthumously appointed him as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong, Emperor Dezong admired his sterling character and again posthumously appointed him as grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子拯，居父喪，有節行，後為伊闕令。

translations.literal: His son Zheng observed mourning for his father with proper integrity and later served as magistrate of Yique.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng observed mourning for his father with proper integrity and later served as magistrate of Yique.

sentences.zh: 會祿山盜河、洛，陷焉。

translations.literal: When An Lushan plundered the He and Luo region, the county fell.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan plundered the He and Luo region, the county fell.

sentences.zh: 而終不受偽官。

translations.literal: Yet Zheng never accepted a false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zheng never accepted a false appointment.

sentences.zh: 賊平，擢太子贊善大夫。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was put down, he was promoted to grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was put down, he was promoted to grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 九齡弟九臯，亦有名，終嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Jiuling's brother Jiugao was also renowned and ended as military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling's brother Jiugao was also renowned and ended as military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 其曾孫仲方。

translations.literal: His great-grandson was Zhongfang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 仲方，生歧秀，父友高郢見，異之，曰：「是兒必為國器，使吾得位，將振起之。」

translations.literal: Zhongfang was born with unusual promise. When Gao Ying, a friend of his father, saw him, he marveled and said: "This boy will surely become a pillar of state. If I ever attain high office, I will raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was born with unusual promise. When Gao Ying, a friend of his father, saw him, he marveled and said: "This boy will surely become a pillar of state. If I ever attain high office, I will raise him up.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，擢進士、宏辭，為集賢校理，以母喪免。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi and hongci examinations, served as collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and resigned upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi and hongci examinations, served as collator in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and resigned upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 會郢拜御史大夫，表為御史。

translations.literal: When Gao Ying was appointed censor-in-chief, he recommended Zhongfang as censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Ying was appointed censor-in-chief, he recommended Zhongfang as censor.

sentences.zh: 進累倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to vice director of the Granary Section.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to vice director of the Granary Section.

sentences.zh: 會呂溫等以劾奏宰相李吉甫不實，坐斥去，仲方以溫黨，補金州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lü Wen and others were expelled for impeaching Chief Minister Li Jifu on unsubstantiated grounds, Zhongfang, as a member of Wen's faction, was reassigned as prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Wen and others were expelled for impeaching Chief Minister Li Jifu on unsubstantiated grounds, Zhongfang, as a member of Wen's faction, was reassigned as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宦人奪民田，仲方三疏申理，卒與民直。

translations.literal: When eunuchs seized commoners' land, Zhongfang submitted three memorials on the people's behalf and in the end obtained compensation for them.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs seized commoners' land, Zhongfang submitted three memorials on the people's behalf and in the end obtained compensation for them.

sentences.zh: 入為度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as director in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as director in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 吉甫卒，太常謚恭懿，博士尉遲汾清謚敬憲，仲方挾前怨未已，因上議曰：「古之謚，考大節，略細行，善善惡惡，一言而足。

translations.literal: When Jifu died, the Ministry of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Gongyi. The erudite Yuchi Fen proposed Jingxian. Zhongfang, still nursing old resentment, submitted a critique: "Ancient posthumous titles assessed the great moral outline and passed over minor conduct; praising the good and censuring the evil — a single word sufficed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu died, the Ministry of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous title Gongyi. The erudite Yuchi Fen proposed Jingxian. Zhongfang, still nursing old resentment, submitted a critique: "Ancient posthumous titles assessed the great moral outline and passed over minor conduct; praising the good and censuring the evil — a single word sufficed.

sentences.zh: 按吉甫雖多才多藝，而側媚取容，疊致臺袞，寡信易謀，事無成功。

translations.literal: Examining Jifu: though multitalented in many arts, he ingratiated himself through flattery, repeatedly reached the highest office, kept little faith and changed plans easily, and accomplished nothing of success.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Jifu: though multitalented in many arts, he ingratiated himself through flattery, repeatedly reached the highest office, kept little faith and changed plans easily, and accomplished nothing of success.

sentences.zh: 且兵兇器，不可從我始，至以伐罪，則邀必成功。

translations.literal: Moreover arms are an ill-omened instrument — they must not be taken up at my initiative. Yet when war was launched as punishment, he always insisted it would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover arms are an ill-omened instrument — they must not be taken up at my initiative. Yet when war was launched as punishment, he always insisted it would surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 今內有賊輔臣之盜，外有懷毒蠆之臣，師徒暴野，農不得在畝，婦不得在桑，耗賦殫畜，屍僵血流，胔骼成嶽，毒痡之痛，訴天無辜，階禍之發，實始吉甫。」

translations.literal: Now within there are thieves among assisting ministers; without, ministers harboring venom like stinging insects. Armies lie wasted in the fields; farmers cannot work the furrows, women cannot tend the mulberry groves. Taxes drain the livestock; corpses stiffen and blood flows; bones and flesh heap like hills. The agony of poisoned wounds cries to Heaven in innocence — the stairway to calamity began with Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: Now within there are thieves among assisting ministers; without, ministers harboring venom like stinging insects. Armies lie wasted in the fields; farmers cannot work the furrows, women cannot tend the mulberry groves. Taxes drain the livestock; corpses stiffen and blood flows; bones and flesh heap like hills. The agony of poisoned wounds cries to Heaven in innocence — the stairway to calamity began with Jifu.

sentences.zh: 又言：「吉甫平易柔寬，名不配行。

translations.literal: He also said: "'Gentle, easy, soft, and lenient' — the name does not match his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "'Gentle, easy, soft, and lenient' — the name does not match his conduct.

sentences.zh: 請俟蔡平，然後議之。」

translations.literal: I ask that the matter be deferred until Cai is pacified, and only then discussed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the matter be deferred until Cai is pacified, and only then discussed."

sentences.zh: 憲宗方用兵，疾其言醜訐，貶為遂州司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong was then waging war and took offense at such ugly impeachment. Zhongfang was demoted to adjutant of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong was then waging war and took offense at such ugly impeachment. Zhongfang was demoted to adjutant of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 稍進河南少尹、鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to vice governor of Henan and prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to vice governor of Henan and prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，李程輔政，引為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Li Cheng entered government, and Zhongfang was brought in as remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Li Cheng entered government, and Zhongfang was brought in as remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 帝時詔王播造競渡舟三十艘，度用半歲運費。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Wang Bo to build thirty dragon-boat racing vessels, estimated to consume half a year's transport budget.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Wang Bo to build thirty dragon-boat racing vessels, estimated to consume half a year's transport budget.

sentences.zh: 仲方見延英，論諍堅苦，帝為減三之二。

translations.literal: Zhongfang attended audience in the Yanying Hall and remonstrated with stubborn persistence. The emperor reduced the number by two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang attended audience in the Yanying Hall and remonstrated with stubborn persistence. The emperor reduced the number by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 又詔幸華清宮，仲方曰：「萬乘之行，必具葆衛，易則失威重。」

translations.literal: An edict was also issued for an imperial visit to Huaqing Palace. Zhongfang said: "The journey of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler must be fully guarded and escorted; if made too easy, majesty and weight are lost.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued for an imperial visit to Huaqing Palace. Zhongfang said: "The journey of the ten-thousand-chariot ruler must be fully guarded and escorted; if made too easy, majesty and weight are lost.

sentences.zh: 不從，猶見慰勞。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow [his advice], yet still received and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him, but still summoned him and offered words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 鄠令崔發以辱黃門系獄，逢赦不見宥。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Hu County, Cui Fa, was imprisoned for insulting a Huangmen official; when an amnesty came, he was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Fa, magistrate of Hu County, had been jailed for insulting a palace eunuch; when a general amnesty was proclaimed, he alone was not forgiven.

sentences.zh: 仲方曰：「恩被天下，流昆蟲，而不行禦前乎？」

translations.literal: Zhongfang said: "If grace covers all under Heaven and extends even to insects, should it not reach before the emperor's person?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang said, "Imperial grace blankets the realm and falls even on crawling things — yet it cannot reach a man standing before the throne?

sentences.zh: 發繇是不死。

translations.literal: Because of this, Fa did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this intervention, Cui Fa was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 大和初，出為福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dahe reign period, he was sent out as military commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dahe era he was posted as military commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 召還，進至左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant of the Loose-Rein Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he rose to Left Regular Attendant of the Loose-Rein Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李德裕秉政，以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu held power, Zhongfang was made Retired Guest of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the Eastern Capital office.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Deyu dominated the government, Zhongfang was sidelined as Retired Guest of the Heir Apparent, serving at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 德裕罷，復拜常侍。

translations.literal: When Deyu left office, Zhongfang was again appointed Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu's fall, Zhongfang was restored to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 李訓之變，大臣或誅或系。

translations.literal: In the Li Xun affair, grand ministers were either executed or imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of Li Xun's coup attempt, senior ministers were killed or thrown into chains.

sentences.zh: 翌日，群臣謁宣政，牙闔不啟。

translations.literal: The next day, when the ministers paid court at Xuanzheng Hall, the gate was not opened.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the ministers came to Xuanzheng Hall for audience, but the gate remained shut.

sentences.zh: 群臣錯立朝堂，無史卒贊候，久乃半扉啟，使者傳召仲方曰：「有詔，可京兆尹。」

translations.literal: The ministers stood disordered in the court hall with no clerks or guards to announce them. After a long while half the doors opened; a messenger summoned Zhongfang and said: "There is an edict — you may serve as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The officials milled about the hall with no attendants to call the roll. Only after a long wait did half the doors swing open; a messenger fetched Zhongfang and announced, "By edict, you are appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 然後門辟，喚仗。

translations.literal: Only then were the doors opened wide and the guard called out.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were the gates thrown fully open and the imperial guard summoned.

sentences.zh: 於時族夷將相，顱足旁午，仲方皆密使識其屍。

translations.literal: At that time, when entire clans of generals and chancellors were executed, heads and feet lay in profusion. Zhongfang secretly sent men to identify each body.
translations.idiomatic: Whole families of generals and chancellors had been exterminated; severed heads and limbs littered the ground. Zhongfang quietly sent agents to identify each corpse.

sentences.zh: 俄許收葬，故胔骸不相亂。

translations.literal: Before long permission was granted to collect the bodies for burial, so the corpses were not mixed up.
translations.idiomatic: Soon permission came to gather the dead for burial, and because of his records the remains were not confused.

sentences.zh: 已而禁軍橫，多撓政，仲方勢笮，不能有所繩劾。

translations.literal: Later the palace guards grew overbearing and often interfered in government. Zhongfang's power was constrained and he could do nothing to hold them to account.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the palace guards ran rampant and meddled in civil affairs; Zhongfang's authority was too narrow to restrain or impeach them.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭覃更以薛元賞代之，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zheng Tan replaced him with Xue Yuanshang; Zhongfang was sent out as governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zheng Tan had Xue Yuanshang take his place and sent Zhongfang out as governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 召入，授秘書監。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was appointed director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 人頗言覃助德裕，擯仲方不用。

translations.literal: Many said Zheng Tan had aided Li Deyu in sidelining Zhongfang and keeping him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Many held that Zheng Tan, abetting Li Deyu, had blocked Zhongfang from useful appointment.

sentences.zh: 覃乃擬丞、郎以聞。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan then proposed appointing Zhongfang as assistant or bureau director and reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan then drafted a recommendation for Zhongfang as an assistant or bureau director and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「侍郎，朝廷華選。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said: "Vice minister is a splendid selection of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said, "Vice minister is one of the court's finest appointments.

sentences.zh: 彼牧守無狀，不可得。」

translations.literal: That provincial governor is unworthy — it cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: That prefect is unfit for such rank — it will not do.

sentences.zh: 但封曲江縣伯。

translations.literal: He was only enfeoffed as Baron of Qujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang received only the nominal title Baron of Qujiang County.

sentences.zh: 卒，七十二，贈禮部尚書，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two. Posthumously appointed minister of rites; posthumous title Cheng ("Accomplished").
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two. The court posthumously made him minister of rites and gave him the posthumous name Cheng, "Accomplished."

sentences.zh: 仲方確正有風節，既駁吉甫謚，世不直其言，卒不至顯。

translations.literal: Zhongfang was upright and possessed moral integrity. After he challenged Jifu's posthumous title, the world did not vindicate his words, and he never rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang was sternly upright and possessed real integrity of character. Because he had opposed Li Jifu's posthumous honors, the age never vindicated him, and he never reached high office.

sentences.zh: 既歿，人多傷之。

translations.literal: After his death, many mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: After he was gone, many grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 始，高祖仕隋時，太宗方幼而病，為刻玉像於熒陽佛祠以祈年，久而刓晦，仲方在鄭，敕吏治護，鏤石以聞，傳於時。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Gaozu served the Sui, the future Taizong was still young and ill. A jade image was carved at the Buddhist shrine in Yingyang to pray for his years; over time it wore dull. When Zhongfang was at Zhengzhou, he ordered officials to restore it, had the inscription cut in stone and reported upward, and the story spread in its time.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, while Gaozu still served the Sui, the future Emperor Taizong lay young and sick; a jade statue was carved at the Buddhist shrine in Yingyang to pray for his life. Years later it had worn dim. When Zhongfang governed at Zhengzhou he ordered it restored, had the deed carved in stone and reported to the throne, and the tale passed into common talk.

sentences.zh: 韓休，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Han Xiu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu came from Chang'an in the metropolitan region of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父大智，洛州司功參軍，其兄大敏，仕武後為鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: His father was Dazhi, adjutant of judicial affairs of Luozhou; his elder brother was Damin, who under Empress Wu served as a drafter of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dazhi had been adjutant of judicial affairs at Luozhou; his elder brother Damin, under Empress Wu, served as a drafter in the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 梁州都督李行褒為部人告變，詔大敏鞫治。

translations.literal: Li Xing'ao, military governor of Liangzhou, was reported for treason by someone in his command; Damin was ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing'ao, military governor of Liangzhou, was denounced for sedition by a subordinate; Damin was ordered to try the case.
