sentences.zh: 或曰：「行褒諸李近屬，後意欲去之，無列其冤，恐累公。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Xing'ao is a close kinsman of the Lis of Zhao. The empress intends to remove him. If you do not set forth his grievances, I fear you will be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "Xing'ao is kin to the Zhao kings of the Li clan, and the empress wants him gone. If you do not record his grievance, I fear you will be dragged down with him.

sentences.zh: 大敏曰：「豈顧身枉人以死乎？」

translations.literal: Damin said: "Would I preserve myself by condemning another to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Damin replied, "Would I save my own skin by sending an innocent man to his death?"

sentences.zh: 至則驗出之。

translations.literal: On arriving, he verified the facts and released him.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he examined the evidence and cleared the man.

sentences.zh: 後怒，遣御史覆按，卒殺行褒，而大敏賜死於家。

translations.literal: The empress later grew angry, sent censors to reinvestigate, and in the end had Xing'ao killed; Damin was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: The empress later flew into a rage, sent censors to reopen the case, and in the end had Xing'ao executed; Damin was ordered to take his own life at home.

sentences.zh: 休工文辭，舉賢良。

translations.literal: Han Xiu was skilled in literary composition and was recommended through the "worthy and good" examination.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu excelled at letters and passed the "worthy and good" provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，令條對國政，與校書郎趙冬曦並中乙科，擢左補闕，判主爵員外郎。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was crown prince, he was ordered to respond item by item on state affairs; together with Zhao Dongxi, a collation secretary, he passed in the second class, was promoted to Left Remonstrance Official, and concurrently served as vice director of the Bureau of Nobility.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was still heir apparent, Han Xiu was told to answer point by point on affairs of state; he and collation secretary Zhao Dongxi both placed in the second class, were promoted to Left Remonstrance Official, and he concurrently served as vice director of the Bureau of Nobility.

sentences.zh: 進至禮部侍郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of rites and drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to vice minister of rites and took charge of drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 出為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as governor of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as governor of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 虢於東、西京為近州，乘輿所至，常稅廄芻，休請均賦它郡。

translations.literal: Guo was a nearby prefecture to the Eastern and Western Capitals; wherever the imperial carriage went, stall-fodder taxes were commonly levied. Han Xiu requested that the burden be distributed equally among other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Guo lay close to both capitals, and wherever the imperial train passed, fodder for the stables was taxed from the prefecture. Han Xiu asked that the levy be spread evenly across neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說曰：「免虢而與它州，此守臣為私惠耳。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue said: "Exempting Guo and shifting the burden to other prefectures — this is a provincial official currying private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue said, "Exempting Guo and dumping the cost on other prefectures — that is a governor buying private goodwill.

sentences.zh: 休復執論，吏白恐忤宰相意，休曰：「刺史幸知民之敝而不救，豈為政哉？

translations.literal: Han Xiu again pressed his argument. A clerk warned that this might offend the chancellor. Han Xiu said: "If a governor, having been fortunate enough to know the people's hardship, does not rescue them — how is that governing?
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu pressed the point again. A clerk warned that he might anger the chief minister. Han Xiu said, "If a prefect knows the people's distress and will not relieve it, what sort of governance is that?

sentences.zh: 雖得罪，所甘心焉。」

translations.literal: Even if I incur offense, I am willing to accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I must offend my superiors, I accept that gladly."

sentences.zh: 訖如休請。

translations.literal: In the end it was done as Han Xiu requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court granted Han Xiu's request.

sentences.zh: 以母喪解，服除，為工部侍郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: Relieved on account of his mother's death; when mourning ended, appointed vice minister of works and resumed drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning; when the period of grief ended he became vice minister of works and again drafted edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Assistant in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍中裴光庭卒，帝敕蕭嵩舉所以代者，嵩稱休誌行，遂拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Palace Attendant Pei Guangting died, the emperor ordered Xiao Song to recommend a replacement. Song praised Han Xiu's integrity and conduct, and Han Xiu was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and Concurrent Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Pei Guangting died, the emperor told Xiao Song to name a successor. Song praised Han Xiu's integrity, and Han Xiu was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and concurrent grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 休直方不務進趨，既為相，天下翕然宜之。

translations.literal: Han Xiu was upright and square, not eager for advancement. Once made chancellor, the realm widely approved the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu was upright and unbending, with no taste for flattery. Once he became chancellor, the realm broadly approved the choice.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉李美玉有罪，帝將放嶺南。

translations.literal: Li Meiyu, a magistrate of Wannian, had committed an offense; the emperor intended to banish him to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Meiyu, a warden of Wannian, had broken the law, and the emperor meant to exile him to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 休曰：「尉小官，犯非大惡。

translations.literal: Han Xiu said: "A warden is a petty official, and his offense is no great evil.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu said, "A county warden is a minor official, and his crime is not a grave one.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷有大奸，請得先治。

translations.literal: Yet the court now harbors great wrongdoers. I ask that we deal with them first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court now shelters great villains. I ask that we punish them first.

sentences.zh: 金吾大將軍程伯獻恃恩而貪，室宅輿馬僭法度，臣請先伯獻，後美玉。」

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of the Golden Crowns Cheng Boxian, relying on imperial favor, is greedy; his residence, chariots, and horses exceed what the law allows. I ask that Cheng Boxian be dealt with first and Li Meiyu afterward.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief of the Golden Crowns Cheng Boxian, trusting in imperial favor, is greedy; his house, carriages, and horses violate the statutes. I ask that Cheng Boxian be punished first and Li Meiyu afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，休固爭曰：「罪細且不容，巨猾乃置不問，陛下不出伯獻，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree. Han Xiu pressed stubbornly: "A minor offense cannot even be tolerated, yet a great scoundrel is left alone. Unless Your Majesty removes Cheng Boxian, this minister dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. Han Xiu argued stubbornly, "A petty crime cannot be tolerated, yet a great rogue goes untouched. Unless Your Majesty removes Cheng Boxian, this minister dare not obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 帝不能奪。

translations.literal: The emperor could not prevail over him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not override him.

sentences.zh: 大率堅正類此。

translations.literal: In general his upright firmness was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In general his steadfast integrity took this form.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩以休柔易，故薦之。

translations.literal: At first Song had recommended him because he thought Han Xiu was gentle and pliable.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiao Song had recommended him because he took Han Xiu for mild and tractable.

sentences.zh: 休臨事或折正嵩，嵩不能平。

translations.literal: In office Han Xiu sometimes corrected Song to his face; Song could not reconcile himself to it.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office Han Xiu sometimes openly corrected Song, and Song could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 宋璟聞之曰：「不意休能爾，仁者之勇也。」

translations.literal: Song Jing heard of this and said: "I did not expect Han Xiu capable of such — the courage of a humane man.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing heard of it he said, "I never thought Han Xiu capable of this — the courage of a humane man.

sentences.zh: 嵩寬博多可，休峭鯁，時政所得失，言之未嘗不盡。

translations.literal: Song was broad-minded and compliant; Han Xiu was sharp and unyielding. On the gains and losses of current policy, whatever he said was never less than complete.
translations.idiomatic: Song was broad and accommodating; Han Xiu was sharp and unyielding. On the rights and wrongs of current policy, he never spoke without saying everything that needed to be said.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗獵苑中，或大張樂，稍過差，必視左右曰：「韓休知否？」

translations.literal: The emperor sometimes hunted in the park or had music played on a grand scale; if it went somewhat beyond bounds, he would always glance at those beside him and say: "Does Han Xiu know of this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sometimes hunted in the park or staged lavish entertainments; if things went a little too far, he would always glance at those beside him and ask, "Does Han Xiu know about this?

sentences.zh: 已而疏輒至。

translations.literal: And before long a memorial would arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a memorial from Han Xiu would arrive.

sentences.zh: 嘗引鑒，默不樂。

translations.literal: Once the emperor looked in a mirror, silent and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor gazed into a mirror, silent and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「自韓休入朝，陛下無一日歡，何自戚戚，不逐去之？」

translations.literal: Those around him said: "Since Han Xiu entered court, Your Majesty has not had a single day of joy — why grieve alone? Why not drive him away?
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said, "Since Han Xiu entered court, Your Majesty has not had a single day of pleasure. Why brood alone? Why not send him away?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾雖瘠，天下肥矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though I grow thin, the realm grows fat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Though I grow thin, the realm grows prosperous.

sentences.zh: 且蕭嵩每啟事，必順旨，我退而思天下，不安寢。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever Xiao Song reports on affairs, he always follows my wishes. When I retire and think of the realm, I cannot sleep in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, whenever Xiao Song reports on affairs he always agrees with me. When I withdraw and think of the realm, I cannot sleep soundly.

sentences.zh: 韓休敷陳治道，多訐直，我退而思天下，寢必安。

translations.literal: Han Xiu sets forth the way of governance, often bluntly to the point. When I retire and think of the realm, I sleep in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiu lays out the way of governance, often blunt to the point of offense. When I withdraw and think of the realm, I sleep at ease.

sentences.zh: 吾用休，社稷計耳。」

translations.literal: I employ Han Xiu for the sake of the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: I keep Han Xiu for the sake of the state."

sentences.zh: 後以工部尚書罷。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was removed from office as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 遷太子少師，封宜陽縣子。

translations.literal: Promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yiyang County.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈揚州大都督，謚曰文忠。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-eight. Posthumously made Great Military Governor of Yangzhou; posthumous title Wenzhong ("Cultured and Loyal").
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight. The court posthumously made him Great Military Governor of Yangzhou and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong, "Cultured and Loyal."

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying he was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子浩、洽、洪、汯、滉、渾、洄，皆有學尚。

translations.literal: His sons Hao, Qia, Hong, Yin, Huang, Hun, and Hui all pursued learning and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Hao, Qia, Hong, Yin, Huang, Hun, and Hui all cultivated learning and moral refinement.

sentences.zh: 浩，萬年主簿，坐籍王鉷家貲有隱入，為尹鮮于仲通所劾，流循州。

translations.literal: Hao was chief clerk of Wannian; charged with concealing assets when inventorying Wang Hong's household property; impeached by metropolitan governor Xianyu Zhongtong; exiled to Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao served as chief clerk of Wannian. When Wang Hong's estate was inventoried he was charged with concealing assets; metropolitan governor Xianyu Zhongtong impeached him and he was exiled to Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪為司庫員外郎，與汯皆以累貶。

translations.literal: Hong served as vice director of the Bureau of Granaries; both he and Yin were demoted on account of connections.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was vice director of the Bureau of Granaries; he and Yin were both demoted through association with the case.

sentences.zh: 洪後為華州長史。

translations.literal: Hong later became chief administrator of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong later served as chief administrator of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 渾，大理司直。

translations.literal: Hun was judicial inspector of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Hun served as judicial inspector in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 安祿山盜京師，皆陷賊，賊逼以官，浩與洪、汯、滉、渾出奔，將走行在，浩、洪、渾及洪四子復為賊禽殺之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan seized the capital, all fell into rebel hands; the rebels pressed offices on them. Hao fled together with Hong, Yin, Huang, and Hun, intending to reach the imperial camp; Hao, Hong, Hun, and Hong's four sons were captured again by the rebels and killed.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized the capital they all fell into rebel hands; the rebels tried to force offices on them. Hao fled with Hong, Yin, Huang, and Hun, intending to reach the emperor's camp, but Hao, Hong, Hun, and Hong's four sons were captured again by the rebels and killed.

sentences.zh: 洪善與人交，有節義，藉甚於時，見者為流涕。

translations.literal: Hong was skilled in friendship and possessed integrity and righteousness; his repute was great in his time, and those who saw his fate wept.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was gifted in friendship and possessed integrity and honor; his reputation stood very high in his day, and those who witnessed his death wept.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以大臣子能死難，詔贈浩吏部郎中，洪太常卿，渾太常少卿。

translations.literal: Suzong, because the sons of a grand minister had died in calamity, ordered posthumous appointments: Hao as bureau director of the Ministry of Personnel, Hong as chamberlain for ceremonials, Hun as vice chamberlain for ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sons of a great minister had died in the calamity, Emperor Suzong posthumously made Hao a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, Hong chamberlain for ceremonials, and Hun vice chamberlain for ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 汯上元中終諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Yin ended his career in the Shangyuan era as remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Yin ended his career in the Shangyuan era as remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 洽，終殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Qia ended as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Qia ended his career as a palace censor.

sentences.zh: 滉，字太沖，以蔭補左威衛騎曹參軍。

translations.literal: Huang, styled Taichong, entered service by yin privilege as military adjutant of the Left Weibei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, styled Taichong, entered office by inherited privilege as military adjutant of the Left Weibei Guard.

sentences.zh: 至德初，避地山南，采訪使李承昭表為通川郡長史，改彭王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he fled south of the mountains; Surveillance Commissioner Li Chengshi memorialized to appoint him chief administrator of Tongchuan Commandery; later changed to adviser of the Prince of Peng's household.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide era he took refuge south of the mountains; Surveillance Commissioner Li Chengshi recommended him as chief administrator of Tongchuan Commandery, and he later became adviser to the Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 初，汯知制誥，當草王玙詔，無借言，銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yin was drafting edicts, he was to compose an edict for Wang Yu but offered no flattering language; Wang harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yin was drafting edicts, he was to write an edict for Wang Yu but put in no flattering phrases; Wang nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及當國，滉兄弟皆斥冗官。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu came to power, Huang and his brothers were all relegated to idle posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu came to power, Huang and his brothers were all shunted into empty posts.

sentences.zh: 玙罷，乃擢殿中侍御史，三遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu left office, Huang was raised to palace censor, and after three promotions became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yu fell, Huang was promoted to palace censor and, after three further steps, became vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 性強直，明吏事，蒞南曹五年，簿最詳致。

translations.literal: Of a forceful, upright nature, he understood administrative affairs; he presided over the Southern Bureau for five years, with records exceptionally detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and upright by nature, he understood administrative work; he ran the Southern Bureau for five years, and his ledgers were exceptionally thorough.

sentences.zh: 再遷給事中，知兵部選。

translations.literal: Promoted again to attendant; in charge of selections in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to attendant, he took charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時盜殺富平令韋當，賊隸北軍，魚朝恩私其兇，奏原死，滉執處，卒伏辜。

translations.literal: At the time a robber killed Wei Dang, magistrate of Fuping; the killer belonged to the Northern Army. Yu Chao'en favored the murderer and memorialized to spare his life. Huang insisted on punishment, and in the end the culprit paid with his life.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a bandit killed Wei Dang, magistrate of Fuping; the killer belonged to the Northern Army. Yu Chao'en shielded the murderer and memorialized to spare his life. Huang insisted on execution, and in the end the man paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 遷右丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 知吏部選，以戶部侍郎判度支。

translations.literal: In charge of selections in the Ministry of Personnel; as vice minister of revenue, concurrently directed the Bureau of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel and, as vice minister of revenue, concurrently ran the Bureau of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 自至德軍興，所在賦稅無藝，帑司給輸乾隱。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide military campaigns began, levies everywhere were without measure, and treasury offices and supply officials engaged in covert withholding and embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide campaigns began, levies everywhere had no fixed limit, and treasury and transport officials skimmed and concealed receipts.

sentences.zh: 滉檢制吏下及四方輸將，犯者痛根以法。

translations.literal: Huang inspected subordinates and transport from all quarters; offenders were rooted out and punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Huang tightened control over subordinates and deliveries from all directions; offenders were ferreted out and punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 會歲數稔，兵革少息，故儲積谷帛稍豐實。

translations.literal: It happened that several years were plentiful and warfare largely ceased, so stored grain and cloth gradually grew abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Several years of good harvests followed, and with warfare largely stilled, stored grain and cloth gradually grew plentiful.

sentences.zh: 然覆治案牘，深文鉤剝，人亦咨怨。

translations.literal: Yet because he reprocessed case files, applied the law with harsh technicalities, and extracted every penny, people also complained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he reopened old files, applied the law with pitiless technicality, and squeezed out every last coin, people complained as well.

sentences.zh: 大歷十二年秋，大雨害稼什八，京兆尹黎幹言狀，滉恐有所蠲貸，固表不實。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twelfth year of Dali, great rains destroyed eight-tenths of the harvest. Metropolitan Governor Li Gan reported the situation. Huang, fearing tax remissions and relief, firmly memorialized that the report was untrue.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the twelfth year of Dali, heavy rains ruined eight-tenths of the harvest. Metropolitan Governor Li Gan reported the damage. Huang, fearing tax remissions and relief, stubbornly memorialized that the report was false.

sentences.zh: 代宗命御史行視，實損田三萬餘頃。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong ordered censors to inspect on site; fields damaged amounted to more than thirty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong sent censors to inspect on the ground; damaged fields totaled more than thirty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 始，渭南令劉藻附滉，言部田無害，御史趙計按驗如藻言，帝又遣御史朱敖覆實，害田三千頃。

translations.literal: At first, Liu Zao, magistrate of Weinan, curried favor with Huang and said no fields in the commandery were harmed. Censor Zhao Ji investigated and confirmed Liu Zao's words. The emperor then sent Censor Zhu Ao to verify again: damaged fields were three thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Zao, magistrate of Weinan, curried favor with Huang and claimed no fields in the commandery were harmed. Censor Zhao Ji investigated and confirmed Liu Zao's account. The emperor then sent Censor Zhu Ao to verify again and found three thousand qing of damaged fields.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「縣令，所以養民，而田損不問，豈恤隱意邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and said: "A county magistrate exists to nourish the people — yet when fields are damaged he asks no questions. Could this be an intent to conceal distress?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and said, "A county magistrate exists to care for the people — yet when fields are ruined he asks no questions. Is this not an attempt to hide the suffering?

sentences.zh: 貶南浦員外尉，計亦斥為豐州司戶員外參軍。

translations.literal: Liu Zao was demoted to acting vice-warden of Nanpu; Zhao Ji was likewise expelled to acting registrar of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao was demoted to acting vice-warden of Nanpu, and Zhao Ji was likewise expelled to acting registrar of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 方是時，潦敗河中鹽池，滉奏池產瑞鹽。

translations.literal: At that very time, floods ruined the salt ponds in Hezhong. Huang memorialized that the ponds were producing auspicious salt.
translations.idiomatic: At that same time floods wrecked the salt ponds in Hezhong. Huang memorialized that the ponds were yielding auspicious salt.

sentences.zh: 帝疑，遣諫議大夫蔣鎮廉狀，鎮畏滉，還乃賀帝，且請置祠，詔號寶應靈慶池。

translations.literal: The emperor was skeptical and sent Remonstrance Official Jiang Zhen to investigate on-site. Jiang feared Huang; on returning he congratulated the emperor and also requested that a shrine be established. An edict named the pool the Baoying Spiritual Celebration Pond.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was skeptical and sent Remonstrance Official Jiang Zhen to inspect the matter. Jiang feared Huang; on his return he congratulated the emperor and also asked that a shrine be established. An edict named the pool the Baoying Spiritual Celebration Pond.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，惡滉掊刻，徙太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he disliked Huang's extortionate harshness and transferred him to Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong came to the throne, he took a dislike to Huang's grasping severity and transferred him to the post of Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 議者不厭，乃出為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated were not satisfied, and so he was sent out to serve as prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated on policy remained dissatisfied, so he was sent out to serve as prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷浙江東、西觀察使，尋檢校禮部尚書為鎮海軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Intendant of Zhejiang East and West, and soon was made Acting Minister of Rites and Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Intendant of Zhejiang East and West, and soon was made Acting Minister of Rites and military commissioner of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 綏輯百姓，均租、調，不逾年，境內稱治。

translations.literal: He soothed and organized the people, equalized land tax and corvée levies, and within less than a year the territory was praised as well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He soothed and settled the people, equalized land tax and corvée levies, and within a year the region was praised as well governed.

sentences.zh: 帝在奉天，淮、汴震騷，滉訓士卒，分兵戌河南。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Fengtian; the Huai and Bian regions were shaken with alarm. Huang trained soldiers and divided troops to garrison Henan.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Fengtian, the Huai and Bian regions were convulsed with alarm. Huang drilled his troops and dispatched forces to garrison Henan.

sentences.zh: 既狩梁州，又獻縑十萬匹，請以鎮兵三萬助討賊，有詔嘉勞，進檢校尚書右仆射，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: After the hunt at Liangzhou, he also presented one hundred thousand bolts of silk, requested thirty thousand garrison troops to assist in suppressing the rebels, received an edict of commendation and reward, was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial hunt at Liangzhou, he also presented one hundred thousand bolts of silk and offered thirty thousand of his garrison troops to help suppress the rebels. An edict commended and rewarded him; he was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 李希烈陷汴州，滉遣裨將王棲耀、李長榮、柏良器以勁卒萬人進討，次睢陽，而賊已攻寧陵，棲耀等破走之，漕路無梗，完靖東南，滉功多。

translations.literal: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou, Huang dispatched assistant generals Wang Qiyao, Li Changrong, and Bai Liangqi with ten thousand elite troops to advance against him. They halted at Suiyang while the rebels were already attacking Ningling; Qiyao and the others defeated and routed them. The transport routes were unblocked, the southeast was secured, and Huang's merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie captured Bianzhou, Huang sent assistant generals Wang Qiyao, Li Changrong, and Bai Liangqi with ten thousand crack troops to advance against him. They halted at Suiyang just as the rebels were attacking Ningling; Qiyao and his colleagues routed them. The grain routes were cleared, the southeast was secured, and Huang's contribution was great.

sentences.zh: 時裏胥有罪，輒殺無貸，人怪之。

translations.literal: Whenever village clerks committed offenses he would execute them without mercy; people found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a village clerk committed an offense, he would have him executed without exception, and people found this strange.

sentences.zh: 滉曰：「袁晁本一鞭背史，禽賊有負，聚其類以反，此輩皆鄉縣豪黠，不如殺之，用年少者，惜身保家不為惡。」

translations.literal: Huang said: "Yuan Chao was originally a clerk who whipped backs; in capturing rebels he held grudges and gathered his kind to rebel. These men are all powerful and sharp-witted figures from the counties and districts — better to kill them and employ younger men, who value their lives, protect their families, and will not do evil.
translations.idiomatic: Huang said, "Yuan Chao began as a back-whipping clerk; when he captured rebels he nursed grudges and rallied his kind to rebel. These men are all powerful, cunning figures from the counties and districts. Better to kill them and use younger men who cherish their lives, guard their households, and will not turn to evil.

sentences.zh: 又以賊非牛酒不嘯結，乃禁屠牛，以絕其謀。

translations.literal: He also reasoned that rebels would not gather and conspire without beef and wine, and so banned the slaughter of cattle to cut off their plots.
translations.idiomatic: He also reasoned that rebels would not gather and plot without beef and wine, so he banned cattle slaughter to cut off their schemes.

sentences.zh: 婺州屬縣有犯令者，誅及鄰伍，坐死數十百人。

translations.literal: In a county subordinate to Wuzhou someone violated an order; punishment extended to neighboring households, and several dozen to a hundred people were put to death on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: In a county under Wuzhou someone violated an order, and punishment extended to neighboring households; several dozen to a hundred people were put to death as a result.

sentences.zh: 又遣官分察境內，罪涉疑似必誅，一判輒數十人，下皆愁怖。

translations.literal: He also sent officials to inspect the territory in divisions; whenever guilt touched even suspicion execution was certain — a single judgment often meant several dozen dead, and subordinates were all filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent officials to inspect the territory in sections; whenever guilt touched even suspicion, execution was certain. A single judgment often meant dozens of deaths, and everyone below him was filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 聞京都未平，乃閉關梁，禁牛馬出境，築石頭五城，自京口至玉山。

translations.literal: Hearing that the capital was not yet pacified, he closed the passes at Liang, forbade cattle and horses to leave the territory, and built five stone fortresses from Jingkou to Yushan.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the capital was not yet pacified, he closed the passes at Liang, forbade cattle and horses to leave the region, and built five stone fortresses from Jingkou to Yushan.

sentences.zh: 毀上元道、佛祠四十區，修撝壁，起建業、抵京峴，樓雉相望。

translations.literal: He demolished forty Daoist and Buddhist shrines in Shangyuan, repaired battlements, raised fortifications from Jianye to Mount Jingxian, with watchtowers and battlements facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: He demolished forty Daoist and Buddhist shrines in Shangyuan, repaired the battlements, and raised fortifications from Jianye to Mount Jingxian, with watchtowers and parapets facing one another.

sentences.zh: 以為朝廷有永嘉南走事，置館第數十於石頭城，穿井皆百尺。

translations.literal: Thinking the court might have a Yongjia-style flight southward, he built several dozen guest mansions in Shitou Fortress, each with wells sunk a hundred feet deep.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting the court might repeat the Yongjia-era flight south, he built several dozen guest mansions in Shitou Fortress, sinking wells a hundred feet deep in each.

sentences.zh: 命偏將丘涔督役，日數千人，涔虐用其眾，朝令夕辦，先世丘壟皆發夷。

translations.literal: He ordered acting general Qiu Cen to supervise the labor — several thousand men each day. Cen cruelly drove the workforce; orders given in the morning had to be finished by evening, and ancestral tombs of former generations were all dug up and leveled.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered acting general Qiu Cen to supervise the work — several thousand men each day. Cen drove the laborers cruelly; orders given in the morning had to be finished by evening, and ancestral tombs of earlier generations were all dug up and leveled.

sentences.zh: 造樓艦三千柁，以舟師由海門大閱，至申浦乃還。

translations.literal: He built three thousand tower ships and, with a fleet, held a grand review through Haimen, returning only when he reached Shenpu.
translations.idiomatic: He built three thousand tower ships and held a grand naval review through Haimen, returning only after reaching Shenpu.

sentences.zh: 追李長榮等歸，以親吏盧復為宣州刺史，增營壘，教習長兵，毀鐘鑄軍器。

translations.literal: He recalled Li Changrong and the others, appointed his trusted official Lu Fu as prefect of Xuanzhou, added camps and fortifications, trained troops in long weapons, and melted down bells to cast military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Li Changrong and the others, appointed his trusted aide Lu Fu prefect of Xuanzhou, added camps and fortifications, drilled troops in long weapons, and melted down bells to cast arms.

sentences.zh: 陳少遊在揚州，以甲士三千臨江大閱；

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou was at Yangzhou and held a grand review with three thousand armored troops along the river;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou was at Yangzhou and held a grand review with three thousand armored troops along the river;

sentences.zh: 滉亦總兵臨金山，與少遊會，以金繒相餉酬。

translations.literal: Huang also mustered troops at Mount Jin, met with Shaoyou, and they exchanged gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Huang also mustered troops at Mount Jin, met with Shaoyou, and they exchanged gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 然滉握強兵，遷延不赴難，而調發糧帛以濟朝廷者繦屬，當時實賴之。

translations.literal: Yet though Huang held a strong army and delayed going to the emperor's aid, the grain and cloth he levied and dispatched to sustain the court came in an unbroken stream — at the time the dynasty truly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though Huang held a strong army and delayed going to the emperor's rescue, the grain and cloth he levied and sent to sustain the court came in an unbroken stream, and the dynasty truly depended on him at the time.

sentences.zh: 李晟方屯渭北，滉運米饋之，船置十弩以相警捍，賊不能剽。

translations.literal: Li Sheng was encamped north of the Wei River; Huang shipped grain to supply him, placing ten crossbows on each boat for mutual warning and defense, so the rebels could not raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng was encamped north of the Wei River; Huang shipped grain to supply him, placing ten crossbows on each boat for warning and defense, so rebels could not raid the convoys.

sentences.zh: 始，漕船臨江，滉顧僚吏曰：「天子蒙塵，臣下之恥也。」

translations.literal: At first, when transport ships reached the river, Huang looked at his staff and said, "When the Son of Heaven suffers dust upon his robes, it is the shame of his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the transport ships reached the river, Huang turned to his staff and said, "When the Son of Heaven is driven into exile, it is the shame of his ministers.

sentences.zh: 乃自舉一囊，將佐爭負之。

translations.literal: Then he himself lifted a bag of grain, and his generals and aides vied to carry it.
translations.idiomatic: Then he himself lifted a sack of grain, and his generals and aides vied to carry it.

sentences.zh: 右丞元琇判度支也，以關輔旱，請運江南租米西給京師。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yuan Xiu was in charge of the Treasury; because Guanzhong was drought-stricken, he requested that Jiangnan land-tax grain be transported west to supply the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Xiu oversaw the Treasury; because Guanzhong was stricken by drought, he requested that Jiangnan land-tax grain be shipped west to supply the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝委滉專督之，而琇畏其剛愎難共事，請自江至揚子，滉主之；

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted Huang exclusively to supervise it, but Xiu feared his stubborn arrogance and difficulty in working together, and requested that from the river to Yangzi Huang would take charge;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted Huang exclusively to supervise the transport, but Xiu feared his stubborn arrogance and found him hard to work with, so he requested that Huang take charge from the river to Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 揚子以北，自主之。

translations.literal: North of Yangzi he would manage himself.
translations.idiomatic: North of Yangzi he would manage himself.

sentences.zh: 滉由是銜琇。

translations.literal: From this Huang harbored resentment toward Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: From this Huang harbored a grudge against Xiu.

sentences.zh: 會琇以京師錢重貨輕，發江東鹽監院錢四十萬緡入關。

translations.literal: When Xiu, because money was heavy and goods light in the capital, dispatched four hundred thousand strings of cash from the Jiangdong Salt Directorate to enter the passes,
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu, because money was scarce and goods dear in the capital, dispatched four hundred thousand strings of cash from the Jiangdong Salt Directorate into the passes,

sentences.zh: 滉紿奏「運錢至京師，率費萬致千，不可從。」

translations.literal: Huang deceived the emperor with a memorial: "Transporting money to the capital costs ten thousand to deliver one thousand — this cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang deceived the emperor with a memorial claiming, "Transporting money to the capital costs ten thousand to deliver one thousand — this must not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝責謂琇，琇曰：「千錢其重與鬥米均，費三百可致。」

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Xiu. Xiu said, "One thousand cash weighs the same as a peck of rice; three hundred [strings'] expense could deliver it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Xiu. Xiu replied, "One thousand cash weighs the same as a peck of rice; three hundred strings' worth of expense could deliver it."

sentences.zh: 帝以諭滉，滉執不可。

translations.literal: The emperor relayed this to Huang, but Huang stubbornly held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relayed this to Huang, but Huang stubbornly insisted it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 至是，誣劾琇饋米與淄青李納、河中李懷光。

translations.literal: At this point he falsely impeached Xiu for supplying grain to Li Na of Ziqing and Li Huai'guang of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he falsely impeached Xiu for supplying grain to Li Na of Ziqing and Li Huai'guang of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，不復究驗，貶琇雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry, did not investigate further, and demoted Xiu to registrar of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry, did not investigate further, and demoted Xiu to registrar of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 左丞董晉白宰相劉滋、齊映曰：「昨關輔用兵，方蝗旱，琇不增一賦，而軍興皆濟，可謂勞臣。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Dong Jin told chief ministers Liu Zi and Qi Ying: "Yesterday when Guanzhong was at war amid locusts and drought, Xiu added not a single levy yet all military needs were supplied — he may be called a toiling minister.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Dong Jin told chief ministers Liu Zi and Qi Ying, "When Guanzhong was at war amid locusts and drought, Xiu added not a single levy yet all military needs were met — he may truly be called a toiling minister.

sentences.zh: 今被謫無名，刑濫人懼，假令權臣逞誌，公胡不請三司鞫之？」

translations.literal: Now he is banished without cause; punishments run wild and people are afraid. Supposing a powerful minister indulges his will — why do you not request the Three Offices to investigate?
translations.idiomatic: Now he is banished without cause; punishments run wild and people are afraid. If a powerful minister is indulging his will, why do you not request the Three Offices to investigate?

sentences.zh: 滋、映不能用。

translations.literal: Zi and Ying could not act on this.
translations.idiomatic: Zi and Ying could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 給事中袁高抗疏申執，滉指為黨與，寢不報。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao submitted a remonstrating memorial in defense; Huang denounced him as a partisan, and the matter was shelved without response.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yuan Gao submitted a remonstrating memorial in Xiu's defense; Huang denounced him as a partisan, and the matter was shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 劉玄佐不朝，帝密詔滉諷之。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanzuo was not coming to court; the emperor secretly ordered Huang to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo was not coming to court; the emperor secretly ordered Huang to admonish him.

sentences.zh: 及過汴，玄佐素憚滉，修屬吏禮。

translations.literal: When Huang passed through Bian, Xuanzuo had always feared him and observed the etiquette due a subordinate official.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang passed through Bian, Xuanzuo, who had always feared him, observed the etiquette due a subordinate official.

sentences.zh: 滉辭不敢當，因結為兄弟，入拜其母，置酒設女樂。

translations.literal: Huang declined, saying he dared not accept this, but then they formed brotherhood; he entered to pay respects to Xuanzuo's mother, and a banquet was set out with female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Huang declined, saying he dared not accept such deference, but then they swore brotherhood; he entered to pay respects to Xuanzuo's mother, and a banquet was set with female musicians.

sentences.zh: 酒行，滉曰：「宜早見天子，不可使夫人白首與新婦子孫填宮掖也。」

translations.literal: As the wine was passed, Huang said, "You should soon see the Son of Heaven — you must not let your lady grow white-haired while a new consort's sons and grandsons fill the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine was passed, Huang said, "You should soon see the Son of Heaven. You must not let your lady grow old in white hair while a new consort's sons and grandsons fill the palace halls.

sentences.zh: 玄佐泣悟。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo wept and came to his senses.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo wept and came to his senses.

sentences.zh: 滉以錢二十萬緡為玄佐辦裝，又以綾二十萬犒軍。

translations.literal: Huang provided two hundred thousand strings of cash for Xuanzuo's travel expenses and two hundred thousand bolts of damask to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huang provided two hundred thousand strings of cash for Xuanzuo's travel expenses and two hundred thousand bolts of damask to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 玄佐入朝，滉薦可任邊事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzuo entered court, Huang recommended him as fit for frontier duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzuo came to court, Huang recommended him as fit for frontier duties.

sentences.zh: 時兩河罷兵，滉上言：「吐藩盜河、湟久，近歲浸弱，而西近大食，北捍回鶻，東抗南詔，分軍外戰，兵在河、隴者不過五六萬，若朝廷命將，以十萬眾城涼、鄯、洮、渭，各置兵二萬為守禦，臣請以本道財賦饋軍，給三年費，然後營田積粟，且耕且戰，則河、隴之地可翹足而復。」

translations.literal: When hostilities in the two He regions had ceased, Huang submitted a memorial: "The Tibetans have long plundered He and Huang; in recent years they have gradually weakened, yet to the west they border Great Qin, to the north they hold off the Uyghurs, to the east they resist Nanzhao — dividing their armies for external warfare, troops in He and Long number no more than fifty or sixty thousand. If the court appoints a general with one hundred thousand men to fortify Liang, Shan, Tao, and Wei, each posting twenty thousand as garrison defense, your subject requests to supply the army from this circuit's revenue and provide three years' expenses. Then establish garrison farms and accumulate grain — farming while fighting — and the He-Long territories can be recovered at a single lift of the foot.
translations.idiomatic: When hostilities in the two He regions had ceased, Huang submitted a memorial: "The Tibetans have long raided He and Huang; in recent years they have gradually weakened, yet to the west they border Great Qin, to the north they hold off the Uyghurs, and to the east they resist Nanzhao. Dividing their armies for external campaigns, troops in He and Long number no more than fifty or sixty thousand. If the court appoints a general with one hundred thousand men to fortify Liang, Shan, Tao, and Wei, posting twenty thousand at each as garrison defense, your subject asks to supply the army from this circuit's revenue and provide three years' expenses. Then establish garrison farms and accumulate grain — farming while fighting — and the He-Long territories can be recovered with ease.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，因訪玄佐，玄佐請行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and consulted Xuanzuo; Xuanzuo volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal and consulted Xuanzuo, who volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 會滉病甚，張延賞奏減州縣冗官，收祿俸，募戰士西討。

translations.literal: Just then Huang fell gravely ill; Zhang Yanshang memorialized to reduce redundant officials in prefectures and counties, collect their salaries, and recruit soldiers for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Huang fell gravely ill; Zhang Yanshang memorialized to reduce redundant officials in prefectures and counties, collect their salaries, and recruit soldiers for a western campaign.

sentences.zh: 玄佐慮延賞靳削資儲，辭犬戎未釁，不可輕進，因稱疾。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo worried Yanshang would stingily cut stored resources, pleaded that the barbarians of the west had not yet provoked trouble and advance must not be rash, and therefore pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo worried Yanshang would stingily cut stored resources, pleaded that the western barbarians had not yet provoked trouble and advance must not be rash, and therefore pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人勞問，臥受命。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch to console him; he received orders while abed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch to console him, and he accepted orders while abed.

sentences.zh: 延賞知不可用，乃止。

translations.literal: Yanshang knew he could not be used and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang knew Xuanzuo could not be used and thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 滉尋卒，年六十五，贈太傅，謚曰忠肅。

translations.literal: Huang soon died at age sixty-five, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and given the posthumous title Zhongsu ("Loyal and Solemn").
translations.idiomatic: Huang soon died at age sixty-five. He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Zhongsu ("Loyal and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 滉雖宰相子，性節儉，衣裘茵衽，十年一易。

translations.literal: Though Huang was a prime minister's son, his nature was frugal — fur coats and bedding he replaced once every ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huang was a prime minister's son, he was frugal by nature — fur coats and bedding he replaced only once every ten years.

sentences.zh: 甚暑不執扇，居處陋薄，取庇風雨。

translations.literal: In great heat he never held a fan; his dwelling was shabby and plain, sufficient only to shelter from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In great heat he never used a fan; his dwelling was shabby and plain, enough only to shelter from wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 門當列戟，以父時第門不忍壞，乃不請。

translations.literal: His gate ought to have displayed halberds in rank, but because the gate of his father's house he could not bear to destroy, he did not request it.
translations.idiomatic: His gate ought to have displayed halberds in rank, but he could not bear to alter the gate of his father's house and so did not request the honor.

sentences.zh: 堂先無挾廡，弟洄稍增補之，滉見即徹去，曰：「先君容焉，吾等奉之，常恐失墜。

translations.literal: The hall originally had no side galleries; his younger brother Hui had slightly added and repaired them — when Huang saw them he immediately had them removed, saying, "Our late father dwelt there; we serve that legacy and always fear to lose or drop it.
translations.idiomatic: The hall originally had no side galleries; his younger brother Hui had slightly added and repaired them. When Huang saw them he immediately had them removed, saying, "Our late father dwelt there; we preserve that legacy and always fear to lose it.

sentences.zh: 若摧圮，繕之則已，安敢改作以傷儉德？」

translations.literal: If it collapses, repair it — that is enough. How dare we rebuild and harm the virtue of frugality?
translations.idiomatic: If it collapses, repair it — that is enough. How dare we rebuild and harm the virtue of frugality?

sentences.zh: 居重位，清潔疾惡，不為家人資產。

translations.literal: Holding high rank, he was scrupulously honest and hated evil; he did not amass property for his family.
translations.idiomatic: Holding high rank, he was scrupulously honest and hated evil; he did not amass property for his family.

sentences.zh: 自始仕至將相，乘五馬，無不終櫪下。

translations.literal: From first taking office to becoming general and chief minister, he rode five horses — not one failed to die in the stable from overwork.
translations.idiomatic: From first taking office to becoming general and chief minister, he rode five horses — not one failed to die in the stable from overwork.

sentences.zh: 好鼓琴，書得張旭筆法，畫與宗人幹相埒。

translations.literal: He loved to play the qin; in calligraphy he mastered Zhang Xu's brush method; in painting he was comparable to his clansman Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to play the qin; in calligraphy he mastered Zhang Xu's brush method; in painting he was comparable to his clansman Gan.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言：「不能定筆，不可論書畫。」

translations.literal: He once said himself: "Without a steady hand one cannot speak of calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Without a steady hand one cannot speak of calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 以非急務，故自晦，不傳於人。

translations.literal: Because these were not urgent duties, he kept them hidden and did not transmit them to others.
translations.idiomatic: Because these were not urgent duties, he kept them hidden and did not share them with others.

sentences.zh: 善治《易》、《春秋》，著《通例》及《天文事序議》各一篇。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, and authored one fascicle each of Tongli ("General Principles") and Tianwen Shixu Yi ("Discussion on the Order of Astronomical Affairs").
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, and authored one fascicle each of Tongli ("General Principles") and Tianwen Shixu Yi ("Discussion on the Order of Astronomical Affairs").

sentences.zh: 初判度支，李晟以裨將白軍事，滉待之加禮，使其子拜之，厚遺器幣鞍馬。

translations.literal: When he first oversaw the Treasury, Li Sheng came as an assistant general to report military affairs; Huang treated him with added courtesy, had his son pay respects to him, and generously gifted him vessels, silks, saddles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When he first oversaw the Treasury, Li Sheng came as an assistant general to report military affairs. Huang treated him with special courtesy, had his son pay respects to him, and generously gifted him vessels, silks, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 後晟終立大功。

translations.literal: Later Sheng ultimately achieved great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sheng ultimately achieved great merit.

sentences.zh: 滉幼時已有美名，所與遊皆天下豪俊。

translations.literal: Huang had already won a fine reputation in youth; those he associated with were all eminent talents under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Huang had already won a fine reputation in youth; those he associated with were all eminent talents under heaven.

sentences.zh: 晚節益苛慘，故論者疑其飾情希進，既得誌，則強肆，蓋自其性雲。

translations.literal: In later years his harsh cruelty grew worse, so commentators suspected he had cultivated appearance to win advancement; once he got his wish he became forcibly unbridled — likely this was simply his nature.
translations.idiomatic: In later years his harsh cruelty grew worse, so commentators suspected he had cultivated an appearance to win advancement; once he got his wish he became forcibly unbridled — likely this was simply his nature.

sentences.zh: 子群、臯。

translations.literal: His sons were Qun and Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Qun and Gao.

sentences.zh: 群終國子司業。

translations.literal: Qun ultimately became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Qun ultimately became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 臯字仲聞，資質重厚，有大臣器。

translations.literal: Gao, styled Zhongwen, was by nature sober and weighty, with the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, styled Zhongwen, was by nature sober and weighty, with the capacity of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 由雲陽尉策賢良方正異等，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: From his post as magistrate of Yunyang he was selected through the Examinations for Worthy and Upright with exceptional grade, and appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as magistrate of Yunyang he was selected through the Examinations for Worthy and Upright with exceptional grade and appointed Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 累遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted through successive ranks to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted through successive ranks to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 父喪，德宗遣使吊問，俾論譔滉行事，號泣承命，立草數千言以進，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: When his father died, Dezong sent envoys to offer condolences and ordered him to compose a narrative of Huang's conduct; weeping he accepted the charge, drafted several thousand words on the spot and submitted them, and the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Emperor Dezong sent envoys to offer condolences and ordered him to compose a narrative of Huang's conduct. Weeping, he accepted the charge, drafted several thousand words on the spot and submitted them, and the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 服除，宰相擬考功郎中，帝為加知制誥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the chief ministers proposed him as director of merit examinations; the emperor additionally made him drafter of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, the chief ministers proposed him as director of merit examinations; the emperor additionally made him drafter of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人、御史中丞、兵部侍郎，號稱職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Secretary, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Minister of War, and was praised as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Drafting Secretary, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Minister of War, and was praised as fulfilling his duties.

sentences.zh: 俄拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Metropolitan Governor.

sentences.zh: 奏署鄭鋒為倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized to appoint Zheng Feng as aide in the granary section.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to appoint Zheng Feng aide in the granary section.

sentences.zh: 鋒苛斂吏，乃說臯悉索府中雜錢，折糴粟麥三十萬石獻於帝，臯悅之，奏為興平令。

translations.literal: Feng was a harshly extracting official; he persuaded Gao to gather all miscellaneous cash in the prefecture, purchase thirty thousand shi of grain and wheat at reduced price and present it to the emperor. Gao was pleased and memorialized to make him magistrate of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was a harshly extracting official; he persuaded Gao to gather all miscellaneous cash in the prefecture, purchase thirty thousand shi of grain and wheat at reduced price, and present it to the emperor. Gao was pleased and memorialized to make him magistrate of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，大旱，民請蠲租賦，臯府帑已空，內憂恐，奏不敢實。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan came great drought; the people requested remission of taxes and levies. The metropolitan treasury was already empty; inwardly anxious and fearful, he memorialized but dared not report the truth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan came a great drought; the people requested remission of taxes and levies. The metropolitan treasury was already empty; inwardly anxious and fearful, he memorialized but dared not report the truth.

sentences.zh: 會中人出入，百姓遮道訴之，事聞，貶撫州員外司馬。

translations.literal: When a eunuch was passing in and out, the people blocked the road to plead their case; the matter reached the throne and Gao was demoted to acting military aide of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When a eunuch was passing through, the people blocked the road to plead their case; the matter reached the throne and Gao was demoted to acting military aide of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改杭州刺史，入拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to prefect of Hangzhou, then entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to prefect of Hangzhou, then entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王叔文用事，臯嫉之，謂人曰：「吾不能事新貴。」

translations.literal: When Wang Shuwen held power, Gao resented it and told others, "I cannot serve new favorites.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shuwen held power, Gao resented it and told others, "I cannot serve new favorites.

sentences.zh: 從弟曄以告叔文，叔文怒，出為鄂嶽蘄沔觀察使。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Ye reported this to Shuwen; Shuwen grew angry and sent him out as Intendant of E-Yue-Qi-Mian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Ye reported this to Shuwen; Shuwen grew angry and sent Gao out as Intendant of E-Yue-Qi-Mian.

sentences.zh: 叔文敗，即拜節度，徙鎮海，入為戶部尚書，歷東都留守、忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Shuwen fell, Gao was immediately appointed military commissioner, transferred to Zhenhai, entered court as Minister of Revenue, and served successively as Eastern Capital Regent and Military Commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen fell, Gao was immediately appointed military commissioner, transferred to Zhenhai, entered court as Minister of Revenue, and served successively as Eastern Capital Regent and military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 大抵以簡儉治，所至有績。

translations.literal: Generally he governed through simplicity and frugality; wherever he went he achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: Generally he governed through simplicity and frugality; wherever he went he achieved results.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部尚書，兼太子少傅。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 莊憲太后崩，充大明宮留守。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died, he was made Regent of Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died, he was made Regent of Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以舊傅恩，加檢校尚書右仆射，俄為真。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, owing to his old tutorship, added him as Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, soon made substantive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong, owing to his old tutorship, added him as Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, soon made substantive.

sentences.zh: 又進左仆射。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年，復為東都留守，卒於道，年七十九，贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing he again became Eastern Capital Regent and died on the road at age seventy-nine, posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent with posthumous title Zhen ("Upright").
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changqing he again became Eastern Capital Regent and died on the road at age seventy-nine. He was posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhen ("Upright").

sentences.zh: 臯貌類父，既孤，不復視鑒。

translations.literal: Gao's appearance resembled his father's; once orphaned he never again looked in a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's appearance resembled his father's; once orphaned he never again looked in a mirror.

sentences.zh: 生知音律，常曰：「長年後不願聽樂，以門內事多逆知之。」

translations.literal: Born with knowledge of pitch and rhythm, he often said, "In later years I do not wish to listen to music, for many things within the household are foreknown against my will.
translations.idiomatic: Born with knowledge of pitch and rhythm, he often said, "In later years I do not wish to listen to music, for many things within the household are foreknown against my will.

sentences.zh: 聞鼓琴，至《止息》，嘆曰：「美哉！

translations.literal: Hearing the qin played, when it reached "Zhixi" he sighed and said, "How beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the qin played, when it reached "Zhixi" he sighed and said, "How beautiful!

sentences.zh: 嵇康之為是曲，其當晉、魏之際乎。

translations.literal: Was it when Ji Kang composed this piece that it corresponded to the juncture of Jin and Wei?
translations.idiomatic: Was it when Ji Kang composed this piece that it corresponded to the juncture of Jin and Wei?

sentences.zh: 其音主商，商為秋，秋者天將搖落肅殺，其歲之晏乎。

translations.literal: Its mode is dominated by shang; shang is autumn — autumn is when heaven is about to shake down and slaughter in severity — is this not the year's twilight?
translations.idiomatic: Its mode is dominated by shang; shang is autumn — autumn is when heaven is about to shake down and kill in severity — is this not the year's twilight?

sentences.zh: 晉乘金運，商又金聲，此所以知魏方季而晉將代也。

translations.literal: Jin rode the fortune of metal; shang is also the sound of metal — this is how one knows Wei was ending and Jin was about to replace it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rode the fortune of metal; shang is also the sound of metal — this is how one knows Wei was ending and Jin was about to replace it.

sentences.zh: 緩其商弦，與宮同音，臣奪君之義，知司馬氏之將篡也。

translations.literal: When the shang string is slackened to match the gong tone — the principle of a minister usurping his lord — one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp.
translations.idiomatic: When the shang string is slackened to match the gong tone — the principle of a minister usurping his lord — one knows the Sima clan was about to usurp.

sentences.zh: 王陵、毌丘儉、文欽、諸葛誕繼為揚州都督，鹹有興復之謀，皆為司馬懿父子所殺。

translations.literal: Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan served in succession as governors of Yangzhou; all harbored plans to restore Wei, and all were killed by Sima Yi and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, Guanqiu Jian, Wen Qin, and Zhuge Dan served in succession as governors of Yangzhou; all harbored plans to restore Wei, and all were killed by Sima Yi and his son.

sentences.zh: 康以揚州故廣陵地，陵等皆魏大臣，故名其曲曰《廣陵散》，言魏散亡自廣陵始。

translations.literal: Ji regarded Yangzhou as the old territory of Guangling; Ling and the others were all Wei ministers — therefore he named the piece "Guangling San," saying Wei's dissolution and ruin began at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Ji regarded Yangzhou as the old territory of Guangling; Ling and the others were all Wei ministers — therefore he named the piece "Guangling San," saying Wei's dissolution and ruin began at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 『止息』者，晉雖暴興，終止息於此。

translations.literal: "Zhixi" means: though Jin rose violently, it ultimately ceased and rested here.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhixi" means: though Jin rose violently, it ultimately ceased and rested here.

sentences.zh: 其哀憤、躁蹙、憯痛、迫脅之音，盡於是矣。

translations.literal: The sounds of grief and rage, agitation and constriction, bitter pain and forced oppression — all are fully present in this.
translations.idiomatic: Every note of grief and rage, agitation and constriction, bitter pain and forced oppression is gathered in this piece.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之亂，其兆乎！

translations.literal: The chaos of the Yongjia era — was this not its omen!
translations.idiomatic: Was this not the omen of the Yongjia catastrophe!

sentences.zh: 康避晉、魏之禍，托以鬼神，以俟後世知音雲。」

translations.literal: Kang, fleeing the calamity of Jin and Wei, entrusted his meaning to spirits and ghosts, waiting for a kindred spirit in later ages — thus it is said."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang, fleeing the calamity of Jin and Wei, entrusted his meaning to spirits and ghosts, waiting for a kindred spirit in later ages — so the tradition runs."

sentences.zh: 洄字幼深，蔭補弘文生，滿歲，參調吏部侍郎，達奚珣以地望抑之。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Youshen, entered the Hongwen Academy by yin privilege; when his year was complete he presented himself for assignment before the Vice Minister of Personnel, but Daxi Xun suppressed him on account of family standing.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Youshen, entered the Hongwen Academy by hereditary privilege. When his year was complete he presented himself for assignment before the Vice Minister of Personnel, but Daxi Xun blocked him on account of his family's standing.

sentences.zh: 除章懷太子陵令，無慍容。

translations.literal: He was appointed keeper of the tomb of Crown Prince Zhanghuai, without a trace of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed keeper of the tomb of Crown Prince Zhanghuai and showed not the slightest resentment.

sentences.zh: 安祿山亂，家七人遇害，洄避難江南，蔬食不聽樂。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, seven members of his family were killed; Hui fled to refuge in the south of the Yangtze, ate plain vegetables, and would not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, seven members of his family were killed. Hui fled south of the Yangtze, ate only plain food, and would not listen to music.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，授睦州別駕，劉晏表為屯田員外郎，知揚子留後。

translations.literal: During the Qianyuan era he was appointed Vice Prefect of Muzhou; Liu Yan recommended him as Supernumerary Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, acting as Yangzi Rear Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan era he was appointed vice prefect of Muzhou. Liu Yan recommended him as supernumerary vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture and acting Yangzi rear commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召拜諫議大夫，與補闕李翰數上章言得失，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Remonstrance Official; with Remonstrance Aide Li Han he repeatedly submitted memorials on gains and losses, and was promoted to Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed remonstrance official. Together with remonstrance aide Li Han he repeatedly submitted memorials on policy, and was promoted to drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 坐與元載善，貶邵州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Because he was on good terms with Yuan Zai, he was demoted to Registrar of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was close to Yuan Zai, he was demoted to registrar of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，起為淮南黜陟使，復為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Hui was raised as Investigative Commissioner of Huainan and again made Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Hui was recalled as investigative commissioner of Huainan and again appointed remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 晏被罪，天下錢谷歸尚書省，而省司廢久，無綱紀，莫總其任，乃擢洄戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: When Yan was punished, the realm's money and grain came under the Ministry of Revenue, but its offices had long lain idle without discipline and no one could gather the task; Hui was therefore promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the Department of Public Finance.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan was punished, control of the realm's money and grain passed to the Ministry of Revenue, but its offices had long lain idle and no one could bring order to the work. Hui was therefore promoted to vice minister of revenue with concurrent charge of the Department of Public Finance.

sentences.zh: 洄上言：「江、淮七監，歲鑄錢四萬五千緡輸京師，工用運轉，每緡度二千，是本倍於子。

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial: "The seven mints of the Yangtze and Huai annually cast forty-five thousand strings of cash for delivery to the capital; labor, materials, and transport cost about two thousand per string — the principal exceeds the product.
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a memorial: "The seven mints of the Yangtze and Huai annually cast forty-five thousand strings of cash for delivery to the capital. Labor, materials, and transport cost about two thousand per string — the cost exceeds the coin produced.

sentences.zh: 今商州紅崖冶產銅，而洛源監久廢，請鑿山取銅，即治舊監，置十爐鑄之，歲得錢七萬二千緡，度費每緡九百，則得可浮本矣。

translations.literal: Now the Hongya smeltery in Shangzhou produces copper, while the Luoyuan mint has long been abandoned. I request that mountains be opened to take copper, the old mint restored, and ten furnaces set up to cast coin — yielding seventy-two thousand strings yearly, with estimated cost of nine hundred per string, so that profit may float above principal.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongya smeltery in Shangzhou now produces copper, while the Luoyuan mint has long been abandoned. I ask that mountains be opened to mine copper, the old mint restored, and ten furnaces set up to cast coin — yielding seventy-two thousand strings yearly at an estimated cost of nine hundred per string, so that profit would exceed cost.

sentences.zh: 江、淮七監，請皆罷。」

translations.literal: The seven Yangtze and Huai mints — I request that all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all seven Yangtze and Huai mints be abolished.

sentences.zh: 又言：「天下銅鐵冶，乃山澤利，當歸王者，請悉隸鹽鐵使。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The copper and iron smelteries throughout the realm are profits of mountains and marshes and ought to belong to the sovereign; I request that all be placed under the Salt and Iron Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Copper and iron smelteries throughout the realm are profits of mountains and marshes and ought to belong to the sovereign. I ask that all be placed under the Salt and Iron Commissioner."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: His proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 復罷省胥史冗食二千人，積米長安、萬年二縣各數十萬石，視年豐耗而發斂焉，故人不艱食。

translations.literal: He also abolished two thousand superfluous clerks and retainers in the ministry, stored grain in the two counties of Chang'an and Wannian to several hundred thousand shi each, and released or gathered it according to whether the year was abundant or lean — thus the people did not suffer hardship in food.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished two thousand superfluous clerks and retainers in the ministry, stored grain in Chang'an and Wannian to several hundred thousand shi each, and released or gathered it according to whether the year was abundant or lean — so the people did not suffer hardship in food.

sentences.zh: 洄與楊炎善，炎得罪，不自安。

translations.literal: Hui was on good terms with Yang Yan; when Yan was punished, Hui did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was close to Yang Yan. When Yan was punished, Hui grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 無何，臯上疏理炎罪，帝意洄教之，貶蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Gao submitted a memorial to clear Yan's guilt; the Emperor suspected Hui had instructed him and demoted Hui to Prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao submitted a memorial to clear Yan's guilt. The emperor suspected Hui had put him up to it and demoted Hui to prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，入為兵部侍郎，轉京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he entered court as Vice Minister of War, then was transferred to Metropolitan Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xingyuan era he entered court as vice minister of war, then was transferred to metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，終國子祭酒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhenyuan era he died as chancellor of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：人之立事，無不銳始而工於初，至其半則稍怠，卒而漫澶不振也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: In whatever men undertake, there is none that does not begin sharply and excel at the start; by the halfway point they slacken somewhat, and in the end grow slack and cannot rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: In whatever men undertake, none fail to begin sharply and excel at the start; by the halfway point they slacken somewhat, and in the end grow slack and cannot rouse themselves again.

sentences.zh: 觀玄宗開元時，厲精求治，元老魁舊，動所尊憚，故姚元崇、宋璟言聽計行，力不難而功已成。

translations.literal: Observe the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong: he strove with keen spirit to seek good government; the senior elders and leading old ministers were all whom he revered and feared — thus Yao Chong and Song Jing had their words heard and plans followed; the effort was not difficult yet achievement was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Kaiyuan era of Emperor Xuanzong: he strove with keen spirit to seek good government, and the senior elders and leading ministers were all men he revered and feared. Thus Yao Chong and Song Jing had their words heard and plans followed; the effort was not arduous, yet achievement was already won.

sentences.zh: 及太平久，左右大臣皆帝自識擢，狎而易之，誌滿意驕，而張九齡爭愈切，言益不聽。

translations.literal: When peace had lasted long, the ministers left and right were all men the Emperor himself had known and promoted; he treated them familiarly and lightly. His will was full and his mind proud, while Zhang Jiuling remonstrated ever more urgently — yet his words were heard ever less.
translations.idiomatic: When peace had lasted long, the ministers at his side were all men the emperor himself had known and promoted; he treated them familiarly and lightly. His will was sated and his mind proud, while Zhang Jiuling remonstrated ever more urgently — yet the emperor listened ever less.

sentences.zh: 夫誌滿則忽其所謀，意驕則樂軟熟、憎鯁切，較力雖多，課所效不及姚、宋遠矣。

translations.literal: When the will is full one neglects what one planned; when the mind is proud one delights in what is soft and familiar and hates what is blunt and cutting. Though one may compare strength in quantity, measured achievement falls far short of Yao and Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the will is sated one neglects what one planned; when the mind is proud one delights in what is soft and familiar and hates blunt remonstrance. Though effort may be great, measured achievement falls far short of Yao Chong and Song Jing.

sentences.zh: 終之胡雛亂華，身播邊陬，非曰天運，亦人事有致而然。

translations.literal: In the end the Hu whelp threw China into chaos and the sovereign himself was cast to the border marches — this is not called Heaven's decree alone; human affairs also had their part in bringing it about.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the barbarian rebel threw China into chaos and the sovereign himself was cast to the border marches. This cannot be ascribed to Heaven's decree alone; human affairs also had their part in bringing it about.

sentences.zh: 若知古等皆宰相選，使當天寶時，庸能有救哉！

translations.literal: If men such as Zhiyang were all chosen as chancellors and placed in the Tianbao era — how could they have saved the realm!
translations.idiomatic: If men such as Wei Zhiyang had all been chosen as chancellors and placed in the Tianbao era — how could they have saved the realm!
